title: Fix Kanban filtering from live board state
accept: Playwright proves q, owner, priority, milestone, multi-tag, and overdue filters; tag=a&tag=b restores a multi-tag filter; route and state changes recompute cards immediately; card click opens the current task in TaskDecisionDrawer; no hardcoded medium option; build, unit, and e2e pass

reason: id collision: allocated T-0001 while plan/plan.json already seeds T-0001..T-0155, so the merged board drew the plan's 'Freeze the PM contract' card under this draft. The allocator is fixed (_plan_id_floor); this created event is retracted rather than edited out of the chain

title: Add Help/Concepts page and remove raw phase enums from user-facing UI
accept: A Help/Concepts route is present in main navigation; it explains AIM's philosophy, barrier, phases, tasks, conversations, approvals/refusals, and how a human acts on an item, with examples and links to relevant routes; every primary user-facing phase label is human-readable (raw values only in tooltips/details for debugging); Barrier tab, descriptions, phase filter, history, refusal rows, and header use the same shared label source; tests cover navigation, terminology rendering, phase label rendering, and no raw enum in visible text; build and related E2E pass

reason: High-priority dashboard review finding: raw phase enum and missing concepts page block human comprehension

title: Kanban filters must derive from the URL, and omitted filters must reset
accept: Playwright proves q, owner, priority, milestone, tag, onlyLate and combined queries each recompute cards immediately; navigating from a combined query to a single-key query resets every omitted filter; two tags are an AND and both survive the URL; leaving and returning to Kanban restores the current URL, not the previous in-memory filters; the VueDraggable column view is read-only and cannot retain stale computed cells; existing card/drawer tests pass

reason: Confirmed by isolated Playwright failure: navigation from ?owner=codex&priority=normal to ?milestone=M2 leaves owner=codex and priority=normal active, rendering 0 of 3 cards

title: Auto-update must defer only for real unsent input or a deliberately scrolled reading history
accept: Live E2E proves a changed record auto-applies with no click or focus when filters are set; filter and select controls never count as unsent text; composer/draft text still defers updates; a deliberately scrolled reading history defers with the scroll reason and preserves position; no global warning is shown; route, query, drawer, selected thread, draft and scroll survive an automatic update; build and all live tests pass

reason: Confirmed by E2E: live update expected 2 cards and remained at 1; deferral reported 'a field has unsent text' on a filtered Kanban page, so filter controls block live data

title: Make every summary signal and task-shaped identifier a deep link or drawer action
accept: Every summary signal deep-links to its owning filtered list and the destination actually applies the filter; task IDs in Attention, Items, Reports, Plan, Gantt, Kanban and Chat open the same TaskDecisionDrawer; blocker IDs open the blocker task or a blocker-filtered list; milestones open a milestone-filtered view; dead-end report identifiers are removed; zero-count signals are visibly non-actions; back/forward preserves route and query; keyboard activation works; Playwright covers one link from each surface and proves the destination is filtered

reason: Leader repeatedly reported that IDs and summary cards look actionable but provide no human operation; this is a cross-page interaction contract, not polish

title: Make every dashboard route usable at 390px without page-level horizontal overflow
accept: At a real 390x844 viewport every route has documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth with no page-level horizontal scroll; the sidebar becomes a drawer or compact rail; tasks/items/reports/plan tables have a deliberate mobile presentation rather than clipped columns; the Kanban board, Gantt chart, Chat reader/composer, and Barrier detail remain usable; every icon-only action has an accessible name; keyboard focus order is visible and sensible; Playwright checks all routes at 390px for overflow and accessible names; desktop E2E remains green

reason: Measured production build at 390x844: all eight routes overflow by 332px; Conversation has 97 focusable elements with no accessible name, Barrier 22

title: Introduce a bounded list-density contract for Items, Reports, Plan, Kanban and Gantt
accept: Use an established Element Plus or >1k-star library pattern rather than a hand-rolled pager or virtual list; Items and Reports have pagination or virtualization with page size in the URL and query preservation; Kanban defaults to a compact card height with acceptance clamped and full text in the drawer; Plan cells are clamped with expandable detail; Gantt has a row-count control and undated items are grouped behind a count/link instead of a tag wall; sticky headers or scroll containment prevent the reader losing column context; Playwright asserts bounded first-screen row/card counts and preserved filters

body:
Reviewer finding on the in-progress Help/phase draft:

The concept dictionary and label extraction are the right shape. One interaction gap remains: `PhaseChip` links to `{ path: '/help', hash: '#phase-...' }`, but the router in `web/src/main.js` has no `scrollBehavior`. With `createWebHashHistory`, navigation is a client-side update, so the page can change without scrolling to the phase row. A chip that says it explains the phase but leaves the reader at the top of a long page is still a dead end.

Please make this verifiable rather than assumed:
1. Clicking any phase chip opens Help and moves the matched phase row into view.
2. Pasting `/help#phase-sealed_divergent` directly lands on that row after the lazy pane mounts.
3. Back/forward returns to the originating page and phase.
4. The test asserts both the heading and the anchor row, not only the route.

title: Define needs-me and receipts-owed from recipient state, not from the presence of a receipt chip
accept: For each viewer, needs-me includes only incoming direct messages addressed to that viewer that require an acknowledgement and are not acked, plus rooms with unread state for that viewer; it excludes messages the viewer sent and messages addressed to another agent; receipts-owed uses the same derived rule as the Chat filter; each thread shows a count/reason for why it needs the viewer; tests cover human, codex and claude-session1 viewers with fixtures containing incoming unacked, outgoing unacked and already-acked mail; clicking the Attention receipts signal lands on the same filtered set

reason: Confirmed from live state: human viewer's unacked list contains codex -> claude-session1; Chat needsMe currently matches any receipt chip regardless of recipient

title: Task drawer must preserve the full seed and must not carry state between tasks
accept: Recording a plan seed preserves title, owner, status, priority, milestone, acceptance, start, due, estimate, tags and blocked-by when the CLI supports them; the drawer resolves the selected task by id from the current board so live updates replace a stale object; decision note and error/result state reset when the selected task changes or the drawer closes; tests create a seed with tags/estimate/dependencies, record it from the drawer, reload and assert every field survives; a second test updates the board while the drawer is open and asserts the drawer shows the current task state

reason: Review found recordTask drops tags, estimate and blocked_by, and decisionNote persists when the drawer switches tasks

title: Playwright must own its server port and never reuse a foreign dev server
accept: E2E never reuses an existing process it did not start; either use a dynamically allocated free port and pass it to both the server and baseURL, or probe and fail with a clear message when the configured port is occupied by a foreign process; the Vite dev server cannot be mistaken for the production dashboard; a test or runner check proves that starting E2E while a foreign listener is on the candidate port fails deliberately or chooses another port

reason: Review run connected to a Vite dev server on 8799 and failed fetching /src/concepts.js; reuseExistingServer makes tests depend on an unowned process

title: Scope action feedback to the row that owns the action
accept: Confirm-receipt success/error appears on the message row that owns it and never on a phase request; phase approve/reject success/error appears only on that request card; busy and result state are keyed by action identity; a failure in one action does not disable or annotate unrelated rows; Playwright covers two phase requests plus a receipt action and asserts the error is visible only on the initiating surface

reason: Verified on source: clicking confirm receipt with no write permission rendered The tool refused this action inside the unrelated Leader Decisions phase card

title: All tag filters share multi-select AND semantics and URL round-tripping
accept: Every surface with a tag filter uses the same multi-select behavior and AND semantics; selecting two tags narrows to items containing both; the URL round-trips repeated tag parameters and restores the selected set; clear resets the full array; Items and Gantt match Kanban instead of keeping a single tag value; tests cover two tags on each tag-filtering surface

reason: Cross-page review: Kanban tag filter is multiple/AND, while Items and Gantt still bind one string and use includes(filters.tag)
Reviewer accepting: isolated and full runs pass every Kanban URL/filter case
Verified against commit 5e21423: omitted-key reset, multi-tag AND, route replace, card identity and computed-column stability all pass
Reviewer accepting: all three live-update tests pass
Verified against commit 5e21423: automatic update without click/focus, draft deferral and scroll preservation all pass

title: Forced update must preserve every deliberate scroll container, including Chat history
accept: A forced update preserves each scroller the reader moved, not only scrollable ancestors of document.activeElement; in Chat, update now keeps .aim-history scrollTop unchanged while adding the new message; composer focus, selection and draft survive; ordinary auto-update and deferred-update paths keep the same guarantee; Playwright extends the reading-position test to click update now and assert the exact scrollTop before and after; a second scroll container in the fixture is preserved too

reason: Reproduced against the running build: .aim-history scrollTop 200 -> 5948 after clicking update now; withReadingPosition only snapshots scrollable ancestors of document.activeElement

title: Add a regression test that the state payload stays JSON-serializable after a task completes
accept: A test creates a task with recorded created and done events, calls the same report/state payload path used by /api/state, and asserts json.dumps succeeds; throughput is a list of ISO date strings and counts, never date objects; the test fails on the previous implementation and passes on the fix; the dashboard state endpoint is exercised once with at least one completed task

reason: Blocking integration defect: after T-0157/T-0158 moved to done, /api/state returned 500 Object of type date is not JSON serializable; fixed directly in aimboard/fold.py and verified HTTP 200

title: Barrier must select the channel it is showing, and keep tab state in the URL
accept: On /#/barrier with no channel query, the first channel shown in the detail is also the active tab and the URL names it; with ?channel=id, that tab is active and its detail is shown; clicking a tab updates the URL and detail together; no state shows one channel's content with zero active tabs; tests assert aria-selected/class state and description content agree

reason: Reproduced on the running build: all five Barrier tabs had active=false while the first channel's descriptions were rendered

title: Deferred updates resume automatically once the obstruction is gone
accept: While deferred, the board keeps checking whether the obstruction still exists; when the draft is cleared/sent or the reader returns a scroller to the top and the digest differs, the update applies automatically and the banner disappears; while the obstruction remains, no update interrupts the reader; tests cover draft-cleared and scroll-returned recovery without clicking update now

title: A phase chip's link must land on the phase row, not the top of Help
accept: Clicking a linked phase chip anywhere in the board puts that phase's row inside the viewport on Help. Measured against .el-main.aim-main (the app scroller), not window: today #/help#phase-cross_examine and #/help produce identical state, scrollTop 0, anchor 1244px below the fold of a 2689px page.

title: Chat 'needs me' must be able to match a channel, and the thread list must show the state it filters on
accept: With the human as viewer, needs me surfaces a channel thread that contains something addressed to the human, and every thread row carries a visible waiting-on-you marker. Today threadNeedsMe returns false for group==='channel' unconditionally and the payload's channel objects carry only gated/id/messages/phase/rule with no unread state; measured live, needs me took 9 threads to 4 and all four were direct threads the human is not a party to, while #hello held an unanswered phase request and was filtered out.

title: Chat message chips must not contradict the record or print the wire format
accept: No rendered chip asserts a demand that the row itself records as satisfied, and no chip prints a transport detail. Today a direct row renders 'acked' and 'receipt demanded' side by side because the chip is derived from ack_required without consulting state, and renders '7350 bytes'. Note the coupling before renaming: threadNeedsMe matches the literal chip string 'receipt demanded', so the meaning must move into the data first.

title: A direct thread must open at what the viewer still owes, not at the first demand ever made
accept: Opening a thread whose earliest receipt demand is answered anchors on the first message the viewer still owes; opening one with nothing owed anchors on the newest message. Today anchorIndex takes the first message carrying the chip regardless of state: on codex to claude-session1 (46 messages, 30659px, 35 demands of which 26 are acked) the pane opens at index 4, a message a day behind the thread's last activity.

title: The palette must be switchable from the UI, and the choice must survive a reload
accept: A control in the shell flips light and dark, the choice is remembered across reloads, and it is reflected in the URL or a stored preference rather than only in memory. The hook is already in place: every colour is a token in style.css with light values on :root and the original dark values verbatim under html.dark, and Element Plus scopes its own dark variables to that same class. The one part that is not a class flip is the markdown body: github-markdown-css ships light and dark as two unscoped stylesheets that both target .markdown-body, so main.js currently imports only the light one and the toggle needs a decision (scoped override, or a dynamically imported stylesheet) rather than a second unconditional import.

title: An item that needs a decision must offer the decision, not only the option to record it
accept: Opening a work item that asks for approval reaches Approve / Request changes / Reject in one click, and the row label names the decision rather than the bookkeeping. Today the action panel's first branch is v-if=!taskRecorded, which short-circuits the decision panel: T-0004 (owner human, status ready, title 'Leader: approve the plan; advance hello past SEALED_DIVERGENT') and T-0035 (status review, high) are both plan seeds, so 'What the leader can do' offers only 'Record this work item' and the row button reads 'record it'. The leader asked for exactly this: 'I want the thing that needs approve to be clickable, go to the detail, and approve there'. taskActionLabel has the same ordering, so the list lies in the same way: it tests 'is it recorded' before 'what does it need'.

title: A channel must say what it is for, and scaffolding must not look like work
accept: The conversation list and the channel header show the channel's topic and its participants, so a reader can tell a transport test from the project. The topic is already in the payload at channels[].topic and is dropped by the conversation view, whose channel objects carry only gated/id/messages/phase/rule. Live evidence for why it matters: the leader was asked to approve a phase transition in 'hello', whose declared topic is 'Transport test: can a Claude Code session and a Codex session reach each other', and which holds 20 recorded tasks; meanwhile 'dev', topic 'aim development: task store, rooms, dashboard', has an empty chain and no task store at all. Four of the five channels are scaffolding (dev, hello, s2-scratch, s2-scratch2, barrier-v0) and none of them says so.

title: Should the leader be required to approve a transition that unlocks nothing?
accept: The leader has ruled, and bin/aim and the Help page agree with the ruling. Today require_leader is called for every advance, so an agent cannot move a channel from Sealed to Committed; but PHASE_RULES gives SEALED_DIVERGENT, COMMIT and SYNTHESIS identical access (read_others=False, channel_say=False, private_say=True), so that edge changes no permission and the approval is bookkeeping. Only SYNTHESIS -> CROSS_EXAMINE ends independence. Option A keeps every edge leader-only and the Help page now says plainly which ones are inert. Option B lets a participant cross an edge that changes no rule, keeping the leader for the edge that does. The cost of B is the simple sentence 'only the human moves the phase', which is currently true and easy to audit.

body:
Measured on the live tree, 2026-09-22, by codex (reporting to the leader).

The leader asked, verbatim: "还有他妈的 hello 这个 channel 是干嘛的."

Answer from the record, not from memory:

- `hello` manifest topic: "Transport test: can a Claude Code session and a Codex
  session reach each other, and can a file-first barrier be enforced by the
  tool?" — phase COMMIT, 71 lines in tasks.jsonl, 1 public log message.
- `dev` manifest topic: "aim development: task store, rooms, dashboard" —
  phase SEALED_DIVERGENT, 0 tasks, 0 messages, no tasks.jsonl on disk.
- `barrier-v0`: 1 task. `s2-scratch`: 0. `s2-scratch2`: 0.

So four of five channels are scaffolding and the one channel carrying the whole
project is named after a smoke test. The channel whose declared topic matches
what `hello` actually contains has never been used.

This is not only a naming problem. The dashboard cannot answer the question
either: `topic` renders in exactly one place in the whole front-end —
`web/src/panes/BarrierPane.vue:36`, inside a descriptions list for the currently
selected channel. `rg -n "topic" web/src/` returns that single hit (allowing the
one in `data.js`). The chat view, the channel picker, and any channel list show
id and phase and nothing about purpose. A reader who opens `/chat` sees `hello`
next to `s2-scratch2` with no way to tell a probe from the project.

Acceptance criteria:

1. Wherever the front-end renders a channel — picker, list, chat header — it
   renders `topic` (the field already ships in `/api/state`; see
   `aimboard/api.py:38` — it is dropped on the client, not by the server).
2. A channel with no tasks and no messages is visibly scaffolding, not a peer of
   a channel with 71 work items. Pick your own affordance (a tag, a section,
   de-emphasis) but the difference must be visible without clicking.
3. `/chat` states what the channel is for above the message stream.

title: A rebuild under an open tab turns every nav click into a silent no-op
accept: With a lazy chunk deleted under an open tab, clicking that route either loads the new build or says so on screen; the URL and the rendered pane never disagree without a visible message

body:
# Repro: a rebuild while a tab is open turns every nav click into a silent no-op

Measured, not inferred. This is the mechanism behind "点击之后没有反应" and it is
silent — the user gets no error and no hint.

## Repro

Build the committed tree, serve it statically, open `#/`, then delete one lazy
chunk (which is exactly what a rebuild does, since `emptyOutDir: true` in
`web/vite.config.js` wipes `web/dist/assets` and renames every content-hashed
file), then navigate:

```
cd /tmp/aim-head/web && npx vite build
python3 -m http.server 8931      # from that dist
# open http://127.0.0.1:8931/#/ , then:
rm dist/assets/ChatPane-*.js
location.hash = '#/chat'
```

## Result

- URL becomes `http://127.0.0.1:8931/#/chat`
- **the pane does not change** — `.el-main` still shows the Attention content
- `pageerror` is **empty**; the only trace is `console.error`:
  `TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../ChatPane-DfLN8GUl.js`
- request log: `HTTP 404 ChatPane-DfLN8GUl.js`, `ERR_ABORTED`

So: the reader clicks a nav item, the address bar changes, the screen does not.
Every route after a rebuild is a dead click until a manual hard reload. The reader
concludes the UI is broken, because it is.

## Why it hits this project constantly

`web/dist` is rebuilt from a dirty working tree while `aimboard serve` is running
from it — I measured that too: at 11:29 `web/dist` was byte-identical to a build
of committed `f4a5af2` (same 20 asset names); at 11:34 it contained
`TaskLink-DAwYZE0t.js`, which exists only in the uncommitted tree. Any tab open
across that boundary has an index.html naming chunks that no longer exist.

## Fix

Vite already dispatches `vite:preloadError` on `window` for exactly this. There is
no listener (`window.__vite_preload_error_handled` is `false`; the console has no
`vite:` trace). The framework-blessed handler is a few lines:

    window.addEventListener('vite:preloadError', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); ... })

but do not make it a bare `location.reload()`. This app's store already has a rule
about not reloading under the reader's hands — `web/src/stores/board.js:57` and the
`deferredReason` path in `App.vue:128` exist precisely to protect unsent text in a
field and a deliberately chosen scroll position. A reload that discards a
half-written message is the same failure the store was built to avoid.

So the handler has to ask the store the question the store already answers:

- no unsent text → reload, and land on the same route (the hash survives a reload)
- unsent text → do not reload; surface the same quiet, non-blocking affordance the
  deferred-update path already renders, with a reload as the offered action

Add `router.onError` as well: a failed lazy component should never leave the URL
claiming one pane while the screen shows another. That is a state the reader
cannot detect from the screen.

## Acceptance

1. With a lazy chunk deleted under an open tab, clicking that route either loads
   the new build or says so on screen. It must not silently do nothing.
2. The URL and the rendered pane never disagree without a visible message.
3. Reload never discards text the reader typed, per the store's existing rule.
4. A test that deletes a chunk and asserts the on-screen outcome, so this cannot
   regress silently — this is the class of bug that is invisible to every check we
   currently run (`npm run test:unit` and `npm run test:e2e` both pass on it).

title: Attention counts plan promises as work, so every signal the leader sees is noise
accept: Every Overdue/Blocked/Review/receipt signal on the landing page counts only items on the record; a seed item is visibly a promise everywhere it is drawn, including rows and counts; T-0004 is either recordable and approvable or not drawn as work

body:
# The Start-here page counts promises as work

The leader's three complaints about the Attention page — "我打开页面看到一大堆东西，
我不知道看什么", "概念太多了", and "T-004 要 human 做东西，但 human 没有可以处理的
方法" — all have this one cause.

## The measurement

`/api/state` ships `tasks` as a single dict of **111** entries. It is two disjoint
universes merged server-side:

    provenance: {'seed only (not yet in the store)': 87, 'store only': 24}
    intersection of plan ids and store ids: []

`plan/plan.json` seeds `T-0001..T-0155`; the task store holds `T-0156..T-0179`.
Claude's own `retracted` event on the store's `T-0001` names the collision:
*"the merged board drew the plan's 'Freeze the PM contract' card under this draft"*
— `channels/hello/tasks.jsonl`, 2026-09-22T02:28:03.908Z. The allocator was fixed
going forward (`_plan_id_floor`); the merge itself was not.

Then every signal on the page is computed over the merged set. Measured against
the live server:

| tile | shows | actually actable by the leader |
|---|---|---|
| Overdue | 4 | **0** — all four are `seed only (not yet in the store)` |
| Blocked | 6 | **0** — all six are seed-only |
| Review | 1 | **0** — T-0035, seed-only |
| Phase requests | 0 | correct |
| Receipts owed | 15 | **4** — 11 are `codex → claude-session1` |
| Plan disagreements | 87 | **0** — one fact, rendered 87 times |

The four overdue rows are T-0004, T-0071, T-0072, T-0074. Every one is a static
string in a JSON file. T-0004 is titled *"Leader: approve the plan; advance hello
past SEALED_DIVERGENT"*, owner `human`, marked `late` — and it cannot be approved,
recorded, reassigned, or moved, because there is no record of it to move.
That is the item the leader pointed at.

`unacked` is `Counter({('codex','claude-session1'): 11, ('human','codex'): 2,
('codex','human'): 2})`. The viewer is `human`. Eleven of the fifteen "receipts
owed" are two agents' correspondence, shown as the leader's work.

## The layout measurement

Viewport 1440x1000; scroller `.el-main` clientHeight **951**, scrollHeight 2186.
Positions inside `.aim-attention`:

    y=   0  h=  83  hero          "ATTENTION / Start here"
    y=  97  h=  63  signals       the six tiles
    y= 174  h= 969  drift-card    "Plan and store disagree on 87 field(s)"
    y=1157  h= 685  columns       "Work needing you now" / "Latest conversation"
    y=1855  h= 207  milestones    "Next milestones"

**The first screen is 100% the drift card.** The only card an agent or the leader
can act on starts 206px *below* the fold. The page's own subtitle is "only what
needs you now; everything else lives in its own pane" — its second card is
everything else, and it is first.

The drift card renders 20 of 87 rows (`board.drift.slice(0, 20)`) and says
"67 more, not drawn here". All 87 are the same shape: `field: "status"`,
`store: null`, distinct ids. One fact — *the plan's seeds were never recorded* —
drawn as 87 rows over 969 pixels.

## The row is the same as the record's row

In `/items`, a seed row and a store row render identically: same columns, same
status tag, same owner, same dates, and the same `late` marker. Measured row text:

    T-0004 Leader: approve the plan; advance hello past SEALED_DIVERGENT
           ready human high M0 2026-09-21 2026-09-21 late 1 T-...

`provenance` is in the payload but is rendered **only inside the drawer**. It is
not in the row, not in any count, and not in any signal. The drawer does say it
well — "provenance / seed only (not yet in the store)" and "nothing recorded: this
is still a plan seed" — so the fix is to move that fact out to where the reader
decides what to click.

## Why this is not "just delete the seeds"

A plan and a record are different kinds of object, and every mature project tool
keeps them apart on purpose: a *baseline* (what was promised) and *actuals* (what
was recorded). Earned-value analysis exists because the two never merge. This
dashboard merges them into one table and one set of counters, which is why the
leader cannot tell what he is looking at — he is looking at a WBS and a board
superimposed.

## Acceptance

1. A count of work is a count of the record. Seed items contribute to no
   Overdue / Blocked / Review signal. If they appear anywhere, they are labelled
   `plan` in the same place the count is.
2. "Receipts owed" means receipts *the viewer* owes: filter `unacked` by viewer.
   Measured target for the `human` viewer right now: 4, not 15.
3. No seed item renders as an actable row without a visible marker. A promise is
   not a work item and must not carry a priority, an owner, or a `late` flag as
   though it were one.
4. The drift fact is stated once, as a sentence, with one action. It does not
   occupy the first screen and it is never above "Work needing you now".
5. Nothing the leader can click leads to a thing he cannot act on. T-0004 is the
   test case: either it is recordable and approvable, or it is not drawn as work.

title: Conversations opens 94,000px above the end and has no unread cursor
accept: Opening any thread leaves the newest message's bottom visible with no click; thread rows carry the viewer's unread count; the view opens on the first unread and never on an already-answered message

body:
# Conversations opens a hundred thousand pixels above the end of the conversation

The leader's words: *"滚动到第一个 unread，默认自动滚动到最新你没做，要用户自己点，
这些都是不可接受的"*. He is right, and it is worse than "a click is needed".

## Measured, live, `/chat` with no parameters

    url                #/chat
    thread that opened claude-session1 ⇄ codex      <-- the leader is not a participant
    messages           112
    scroller           .aim-history, clientHeight 554, scrollHeight 100,119
    scrollTop          10,379
    gap to the bottom  93,972 px
    anchor             message index 8 of 112
    thread rows        unread markers: none, on any row

So the landing state of the page is: a conversation between two agents, opened at
its eighth message, with the newest message 94,000 pixels below the fold, and no
row anywhere saying what is unread.

The reader's own thread is worse than the agent one. `codex ⇄ human` — the leader's
mail — sits at the bottom of the sidebar with no marker at all, while
`/api/state.unacked` says two messages addressed to the `human` viewer are awaiting
a receipt. The page has the fact and does not draw it.

## Root cause, read out of `web/src/panes/ChatPane.vue`

`anchorIndex` (line 168) picks, in this order:

1. the **first** message carrying the chip `'receipt demanded'` — line 171
2. otherwise `msgs.length - room.unread[viewer]` — rooms only, line 174
3. otherwise `msgs.length - 1`

and `scrollToAnchor` (line 190) then puts that message's **top** at the scroller's
top, minus 12px. Two consequences:

- Rule 1 wins over everything. On this thread the first `receipt demanded` chip is
  message 8, so the newest message never gets a chance. This is T-0174, the same
  function; the leader's complaint and T-0174 are one bug and I am folding them
  together rather than paying for two reviews.
- Rule 3 is not "go to the bottom" either. Scrolling the last message's *top* into
  view leaves the reader at the start of the newest message with the rest of it
  below, and on a one-message thread (`#hello`: scrollHeight 584 = clientHeight 584)
  it happens to look right, which is why this survived. `jumpToEnd()` (line 213)
  exists as a button and is the only thing that actually reaches the end. That is
  the click the leader is objecting to.

## The thing the fix needs, and does not have

There is no per-viewer read cursor for channels or direct messages. `unread` is
computed for **rooms only** — `aimboard/fabric.py:82`, surfaced by
`aimboard/gate.py:125`. Channels and DMs have no read state at all, so "the first
unread message" is not currently computable for the two thread kinds the leader
actually reads.

What *does* exist, on the record, and is being ignored:

- `unacked` in `/api/state` — mail whose receipt the recipient has not given.
  For the `human` viewer: `[('codex','human') x2]`.
- `MAIL_STATE_TYPE = { acked: 'success', claimed: 'warning', unread: 'info' }` —
  `web/src/theme.js:31` — a three-state receipt vocabulary that already exists and
  is spent on chips.

So the honest fix has two parts, and part one can land today:

1. **No new state:** land on the newest message, bottom-aligned, automatically.
   Use `unacked` for DMs: open on the first message addressed to the viewer that
   has no receipt yet.
2. **New state, if you want real unread for channels:** a read cursor on the
   record. Proposed verb, in the existing style:

       aim read --as human --channel hello --through 20260922T034308.913Z-codex

   appending a `read` event to the channel's chain, like every other cursor in this
   fabric. Why on the record rather than in `localStorage`: it survives a device
   change, it is auditable, and — the part worth having — it lets an agent see that
   the leader has read its report. Right now an agent cannot tell "no reply" from
   "not read", which is a real cost in this project.

   If you conclude a browser-local cursor is the right call for this, say so in the
   code with the reason. Do not do the weaker thing silently; that is the failure
   this repo is built to catch.

## Acceptance

1. Opening `/chat` with no `thread` parameter does not open a conversation the
   viewer is absent from when a conversation involving the viewer is unread.
2. Opening any thread leaves the newest message's bottom visible: gap to bottom
   equals 0. Today it is 93,972. No click, no "newest" button.
3. With unread on the record, the view opens on the **first** unread, marks the
   boundary visibly, and never opens on an already-answered message.
4. Every thread row shows the viewer's unread count, so the list is readable
   without opening each item. `codex ⇄ human` must not render as quiet.
5. Auto-scroll happens on open only. It does not fight the reader: if someone is
   scrolled up, or has unsent text, the existing deferral rule in
   `web/src/stores/board.js:57` governs. Never scroll under the reader's hands.

Folded into T-0181. The leader raised this himself: opening a thread lands on an already-answered message and the newest message is 93,972px below. Both are the same function — anchorIndex, web/src/panes/ChatPane.vue:168 — whose first rule is 'the first message carrying the receipt demanded chip' and whose fallback scrolls the last message's top into view rather than the bottom. One fix, one review, so this card is closed as a sub-case rather than queued separately.

reason: folded into T-0181: same function (anchorIndex), same fix; the leader raised it directly and it is covered by that card's acceptance criteria 2 and 3

title: Latest conversation's receipt count is a five-row window, not the record
accept: The receipt count is computed from the whole payload and does not change when the display window changes; the collapsed row is dated by the latest receipt and can be opened to see which messages it stands for

body:
# "4 receipts arrived" is a count of a five-row window, not a count of receipts

Raised because claude-session1 reported this expression as doing nothing. Its
analysis is wrong, and the defect that is actually there is a different one. Both
halves matter: if we act on the wrong diagnosis we will restructure working code
and write a test that enshrines wrong behaviour.

## What was claimed, and why it is wrong

Claim: *"`rows` is built by `board.conversationRows.slice(-5).reverse()`, and the
getter returns freshly-constructed objects, so `receipts` holds copies, never the
elements of `rows`, and `row === first` cannot match for any `row`. The collapse
is total rather than partial, so the count is folded into a row that is then
dropped."*

`Array.prototype.filter` returns a new **array** of the **same element
references**. Freshly-constructed objects in `rows` does not matter: identity is
preserved *within* `rows`, so `receipts[0] === rows[i]` for the matching `i`. The
filter keeps that one row and the map attaches the count to it. Measured on the
live board (`HEAD` = `d20a67b`, `web/` clean, `dist` committed, viewer `human`):

    /#/attention  ->  Latest conversation card renders 2 rows
    row 1: codex  claude-session1 ⇄ codex  T-0181 filed (leader-raised)…  direct  03:46
    row 2: claude-session1  claude-session1 ⇄ codex  4 receipts arrived   direct  03:46

So the count is rendered and the collapse is partial, which is what the code says
it does. There is no identity bug. Do not restructure it on that argument.

## The defect that is there

    web/src/panes/OverviewPane.vue:64
      const rows = board.conversationRows.slice(-5).reverse()
      const receipts = rows.filter((row) => receiptRe.test(row.subject || ''))
      ...
      subject: `${receipts.length} receipts arrived`

`receipts` is drawn from a **five-row window**, so `receipts.length` is the number
of receipt rows that happen to be inside the last five rows. It is capped at 5 and
it is a count of what is visible, not of what arrived.

Measured, same payload:

    conversation.mail tail:
      03:46:37.085  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:37.144  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:37.206  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:37.266  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:37.329  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:37.395  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:37.479  RECEIPT for …codex
      03:46:59.725  T-0181 filed (leader-raised)…

    seven receipts arrived. The card says "4 receipts arrived".

The number the reader is shown is wrong by three, right now, on the landing page,
for the ordinary case. Any burst larger than the window is under-reported by an
unknown amount, and the reader has no way to know that the number is a property of
the window rather than of the record.

Two smaller consequences of the same expression:

- The collapsed row keeps the **first** receipt's `ts` and `body` while claiming N
  arrived. In this burst all seven are inside 394ms so nothing looks wrong; if
  they spread over an hour the card dates the whole group to its earliest member.
- The collapsed row has no path to the receipts it stands for. The reader is told
  "4 receipts arrived" and cannot see which four.

## Acceptance

1. The number is the number of receipts that arrived, counted from the payload, not
   from the window. It must not change when the window size changes, and a test
   must fail if `receiptCount` is derived from a slice.
2. The collapsed row is dated by the **latest** receipt in the group, not the first.
3. The collapsed row leads somewhere: opening it shows which messages were
   receipted, or it opens the thread. A count the reader cannot expand is the dead
   end the leader objects to.

title: A tile that says needs-action links to itself and moves nothing
accept: No control links to a fragment of the page it is already on, and every fragment link changes scrollTop when its target is below the fold

body:
# A tile that says "needs action" links to itself and moves nothing

Measured on the live board, `HEAD` = `d20a67b`, viewer `human`, viewport 1440x1000.

    /#/attention, the sixth signal tile:
      reads   "87  Plan disagreements  needs action"
      href    "#/attention#drift"
      click   scrollTop of .el-main: 0 -> 0
      url     #/attention#drift

The reader is told something needs action, clicks it, and nothing happens. The
fragment goes into the address bar and the page does not move.

## Root cause

Same mechanism as T-0171, measured there three ways and now measured here from a
different surface: the router has no `scrollBehavior`, the page's scroller is
`.el-main.aim-main` rather than `window`, so a fragment on a lazy route is never
honoured. `#/attention#drift` is the strongest form of it — a **self**-link on the
pane that is already open.

Two things make this worse than a generic anchor bug:

- It is on the leader's landing page, in the row of tiles that exists to tell him
  what to do. It is the one tile whose destination is inside the page the reader is
  already standing on, so the "nothing happened" reading is the only possible one.
- Even if the anchor worked, the destination is the drift card, which T-0180
  measures at y=174 h=969 — usually already on screen. So the tile cannot be
  satisfied by fixing the scroll alone: a count of 87 promises that the record does
  not hold is not a list the leader can act on, and the tile should either point at
  the plan/record comparison the count is really about, or not be a link.

`web/src/panes/OverviewPane.vue` builds the signal tiles; the zero-valued one is
already a plain `div` with `aria-disabled`, so the shape for "this is not a
destination" exists in the same file.

## Acceptance

1. No control on the landing page links to a fragment of the page it is already on.
   A tile whose subject is in another pane links to that pane; a tile whose subject
   is the current pane's own card either scrolls to it reliably or is not a link.
2. A fragment link anywhere in the app lands on its target: the router either sets
   `scrollBehavior` or the app scrolls `.el-main` explicitly. Measured: `scrollTop`
   must change when the target is below the fold.
3. A test asserts the destination of every signal tile resolves to either a
   different route or a fragment whose target is off-screen before the click, so a
   self-link that moves nothing cannot be added again.

Fixes T-0171 at the root as well: same mechanism, one implementation.

# T-0159's claim does not hold on the landing page: milestone identifiers are still dead text

The commit that closes this card says, in its own message: *"Every id the board
draws is now a way into the thing it names, and every summary that says something
needs action lands on the thing that needs it."* Measured at that commit
(`d20a67b`, viewer `human`, 1440x1000), one class of id was missed.

    /#/plan        M6 M0 M1 M2 M3 M4 M5 M7 M8 M9   all render as A.aim-task-link
                                                    -> #/items?milestone=Mx
    /#/attention   "Next milestones" card: M0, M1, M2
                   interactive wrapper inside the row: null, for all three rows
                   links in the card: exactly one, "full plan" -> #/plan

So the same identifier is a way in on `/plan` and dead text on the landing page —
and I checked there is no test for the landing page's milestone rows; `links.spec.js`
asserts the milestone link on the plan side only (`links.spec.js:154`,
`links.spec.js:203`).

`/gantt` is worth checking at the same time: an earlier audit measured the Gantt's
"items with no dates, so no bar" tag wall as eight renderings of `T-0171`-style ids
as plain text with zero live identifiers on the whole route. I have a reviewer
re-measuring that pane now and will file it separately if it still holds; do not
close this card on the milestone rows alone without looking at the Gantt.

## Acceptance

The card is done when a check exists that walks every route, collects every
`T-\\d+|M\\d+|D\\d+|R\\d+` token in the rendered text, and fails if any of them is
neither inside a link nor inside the drawer control. That is the only form of this
assertion that cannot be satisfied by fixing exactly the panes someone remembered
— which is what happened here, on the fifth different pane, after four rounds.

# Corrections to this card. My diagnosis was wrong and the prescription I sent was wrong.

I filed this from reading `TaskDecisionDrawer.vue` instead of running it. Both halves
of the stated cause are false. Recorded here rather than edited out of the card,
because the record is the point.

## What I claimed, and what is actually true

Claimed: *"the action panel's first branch is `v-if="!taskRecorded"`, which
short-circuits the decision"* and *"`taskActionLabel` has the same ordering, which is
why every Attention row read 'record it'."*

`TaskDecisionDrawer.vue:33-35`:

    const taskRecorded = computed(() => …)
    const isReview = computed(() => taskRecorded.value && props.task?.status === 'review')

`isReview` **already requires** `taskRecorded`. The two branches are mutually
exclusive, so their order cannot short-circuit anything. `taskActionLabel`
(`OverviewPane.vue:99`) is the same: it gates on `taskRecorded` and returns
`'record it'` for a seed, `'accept or return'` for a recorded `review` item. Both
are correct as written.

Measured at `d20a67b`, viewer `human`, opening rows from the id column of `#/items`:

    T-0004  seed, status ready,  owner human, tags decision+blocker, due 2026-09-21 (late)
            -> drawer "T-0004", buttons: ["Record this work item"]
    T-0035  seed, status review
            -> drawer "T-0035", buttons: ["Record this work item"]
    T-0176  on the record, status ready
            -> drawer "T-0176", buttons: ["Start doing", "Assign to me"]

The seed behaviour is **deliberate and already tested**, and the test is right:
`web/tests/links.spec.js:181` — *"Alpha is a plan seed, so that is 'record it', not the
review decisions -- offering a decision for work that has never been recorded is the
control that lies."*

So the live behaviour is not a bug. The leader's complaint is still real — T-0004 is
titled "Leader: approve the plan", owned by `human`, tagged `decision`, and marked
`late`, and he cannot decide it — but its cause is that the plan's promises are drawn
as work. That is `T-0180`, criteria 3 and 5, not this card.

## What is genuinely defective here, and all that is left of this card

**The one flow the leader asked for has no test.** The strings `Approve`,
`Request changes` and `Reject` appear **nowhere** under `web/tests/`. The only
assertions about the action panel are:

    boards.spec.js:153  expect(.aim-action-panel h4).toHaveText('What the leader can do')
    boards.spec.js:154  expect(.aim-action-panel .el-button).first() toBeVisible
    links.spec.js:183   expect(.aim-action-panel).toContainText('Record this work item')

`.el-button` **first** is visible is satisfied by any button at all. So
`TaskDecisionDrawer.vue:208/213/218` — Approve, Request changes, Reject — is
unexecuted code, and if it broke tomorrow the suite would stay green. That is the
same "code that reads as correct and was never run against a case where it matters"
this project keeps measuring, and it sits on precisely the flow the leader has now
complained about twice.

Also worth pinning while it is cheap: `T-0176` itself renders `Start doing` and
`Assign to me`. Neither the label nor the panel is checked against a table of
expected values, so they can drift apart silently.

## Acceptance, narrowed to this

1. A test drives a **recorded** item in `review` through the drawer and asserts the
   emitted argv: Approve → `task move … --to done`; Request changes → `--to doing`;
   Reject → `--to dropped` **with a reason**, since `bin/aim:1448` refuses
   `--to dropped` without one, so Reject must collect input rather than fire blind.
2. A test asserts Approve surfaces the standing blocker rather than failing after the
   click: `bin/aim:1441` refuses `--to done` while any `blocked_by` item is not done.
3. A table-driven test over every (status × provenance) pair asserting the row's
   label and the drawer's first panel agree, so `taskActionLabel` and the panel
   cannot drift.
4. A test pins the current deliberate behaviour: a seed that claims a decision is
   offered only "record it", with the reason quoted from `links.spec.js:181`.

Not in scope: changing the seed behaviour, and making seed items decidable. See
T-0180.

title: The task drawer cannot open, and each attempt leaves a blocking overlay
accept: Clicking any work item on any surface opens the drawer; a render error inside the drawer leaves no overlay behind and the page stays navigable; a test covers opening from every surface and the error path

body:
# The task drawer cannot open at all, and each attempt leaves a blocking overlay

Severity: the board is unusable until a manual reload. This is live on the served
bundle right now, and it is on the one interaction the leader uses to act on
anything.

## Repro, measured

Live board at `http://127.0.0.1:8799` (the only board currently running; see the
note at the end), viewer `human`, viewport 1440x1000.

Click any work item, on any surface:

    #/attention  "Work needing you now" -> T-0156   drawer 0, overlay 1
    #/attention  promise card           -> T-0004   drawer 0, overlay 1
    #/kanban     a card                             drawer 0, overlay 1
    #/items      a row                              drawer 0, overlay 1

And the reader cannot get away from it:

    element at the centre of the viewport before the click:  el-card__header
    element at the centre of the viewport after the click:   DIV.el-overlay.is-drawer.el-modal-drawer
    drawerCount: 0        overlayVisible: true
    navReachable: false   (the nav is under the overlay)
    clicking the nav through the overlay: URL stays #/attention

So the sequence for the leader is: click a work item → the screen freezes → every
click, including the nav, is swallowed → reload the page and lose your place. Every
time. And the overlay survives a route change, so once it happens the whole board is
bricked, not just the pane you were on.

## Root cause

`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'decision')`, thrown during
render, twice per click:

    web/src/components/TaskDecisionDrawer.vue:239
      <template v-else-if="action.decision">

`action` is **not defined anywhere in this component**. `rg -n "const action"` over
that file returns nothing. The component defines `decision` instead (line 38:
`const decision = computed(() => needsDecision(props.task))`), and the module it now
imports exports a *function* named `taskAction` (`web/src/composables/taskAction.js:77`).
So a rename left a stale reference: the template reads a name the component never
binds. In a Vue 3 template an unbindable identifier resolves through the render proxy
to `undefined`, hence `undefined.decision`.

`HEAD` does not have this — `git show HEAD:web/src/components/TaskDecisionDrawer.vue`
contains no `action.decision`. It is in the **uncommitted** working tree
(`git status`: ` M web/src/components/TaskDecisionDrawer.vue`, plus the untracked
`web/src/components/PromiseTag.vue` and `web/src/composables/taskAction.js`), and that
uncommitted tree is what `web/dist` was built from and what is being served.

## The part that matters more than the typo

A render error must not be able to leave a full-screen modal overlay with no dialog
in it. The overlay mounts before the panel renders, so a failure inside the panel
strands it. That failure mode is strictly worse than the bug: a broken panel is a bad
panel, a blocking invisible overlay is a bricked board, and the reader has no way to
tell what happened or how to recover other than guessing that a reload will help.

## Acceptance

1. Clicking any work item on any surface opens the drawer. Measured: `drawer` 1 and
   `overlay` 1 with a visible panel, on `#/attention`, `#/kanban`, `#/items`, `#/gantt`.
2. A render error inside the panel leaves **no** overlay behind, and the page remains
   navigable. Test it by making the panel throw on purpose: the assertion is
   `document.querySelectorAll('.el-overlay').length === 0` and the nav still responds.
3. A test asserts the drawer opens from every surface that can open it, since a single
   shell-mounted component failing takes down all of them at once — which is what just
   happened.
4. No uncommitted build is served to the leader. Either the served bundle is built from
   a commit, or the page says which revision it is and whether the tree was dirty. The
   leader has now been handed a bricked board twice by uncommitted work, and neither
   time could he tell what he was looking at.

## Note on the running board

`8777` is dead — I measured `curl http://127.0.0.1:8777/` returning nothing and no
process listening. Only `8799` is up, started with `--refresh 20 --allow-write` and
defaulting to `--as human`. So the board above is the one the leader has.

title: The D and R prefixes and the raw phase enums have no way in, and Help has nothing to land on
accept: See the card body for the acceptance criteria

body:
# The prefixes Help documents have no way in, and Help has nothing to land on

Measured by a reviewer on the live board, viewport 1280x800, `human`.

**Dead identifiers in the panes.** `#/plan` renders decision ids `D5`, `D6`, `D7` as
`<b>` text with no link (`PlanPane.vue:114`), and the risks table's 13 first cells
`R1`..`R13` with **0 anchors and 0 buttons** in the table body
(`PlanPane.vue:100`, a bare `prop="id"` column). `#/barrier` renders 5 refusal rows
containing `REFUSED: cannot publish a work item while the channel is in
SEALED_DIVERGENT.` where `closest('a')` is `null` for every row and the phase cell is
a plain `<span>`. Contrast `PlanPane.vue:80-81`, where milestone ids **do** link.

**And there is nothing to link to.** Help's identifier rows carry **no `id`
attribute** — all four rows report `id: ""` — so even if a `D` or an `R` were made a
link there is no element on Help for it to resolve to. `/barrier` has 13 in-main links
to `/help`, all of them `PhaseChip`s, none on a refusal row.

So the reader sees `D7` in the decisions table and `SEALED_DIVERGENT` inside a refusal,
and neither is a way to the explanation. He has to already know the nav has a "Help &
concepts" item, go there, and find the row himself.

T-0159 was scoped to `T-` ids via `TaskLink`. The `M`/`D`/`R` vocabulary and the raw
phase enums are precisely the set it did not reach — and Help documents exactly that
set, which is why the gap is invisible from the Help side.

## Acceptance

1. Every rendered `T#`/`M#`/`D#`/`R#` and every raw phase enum in user-facing text is
   inside an `<a>` whose `href` resolves to an element id present in the DOM, and
   clicking it brings that element into the viewport.
2. Help's identifier rows and its phase rows carry stable ids.
3. A test walks each route, collects every such token in the rendered text, and fails
   on any that is neither inside a link nor inside the drawer control. The previous
   round fixed exactly the panes someone remembered; four rounds in, this assertion is
   the only form that keeps holding.

title: Help is a 4564px wall with no contents, and never says what any pane is for
accept: See the card body for the acceptance criteria

body:
# Help is a 4564px wall with no table of contents, and never says what any pane is for

Measured by a reviewer, viewport 1280x800: `#/help` is **4564px** tall inside a
**751px** scroller. The identifiers section begins **1809px** below the pane top; the
glossary **2943px**. There is no table of contents and no in-page navigation.

Its text is 11,956 characters and **never contains the words "Kanban", "Gantt" or
"Conversations"**. The five cards are Concepts / Phases / State machine / Identifiers /
Glossary — there is no pane directory at all. Help's own promise
(`HelpPane.vue:42`) is *"This page explains what the dashboard is showing"*, and the one
thing a lost reader needs is a map of the panes.

The per-pane purpose text already exists: every `web/src/views/*.js` carries a `hint`,
and it is rendered only once you have already arrived, at `App.vue:138`. Help never
reads it. The nav does not show it either (`App.vue:53-67`), which is why "Kanban" and
"Gantt" name tools rather than purposes, and "Audit & barrier" and "Plan & risks" each
name two things.

Element Plus `ElAnchor`/`ElAnchorLink` ships in the installed `element-plus@2.14.6`
(27,778 stars) and supports a `container` prop, so the TOC does not need hand-rolling.

Also measured while checking the identifiers section: the phases card's "usually next"
cell renders a bare `COMMIT`/`SYNTHESIS` with no label and no link
(`HelpPane.vue:91`) while the transition table directly below it uses English
`PhaseChip`s. The raw enum survives in the one place T-0156 was about.

## Acceptance

1. Help opens with a map of the panes: every route in the shell, its purpose sentence,
   and a link to it. The sentences come from `views/*.js`, not from a second copy.
2. A reader can reach any section of Help in one click from the top, and the current
   section is indicated. Scroll-spy comes from Element Plus, not from a hand-rolled
   listener.
3. No raw protocol enum renders in Help's own prose without its English label beside it.

title: Help's T row teaches the wrong model of the 115 ids it counts
accept: See the card body for the acceptance criteria

body:
# Help's `T-` row teaches the wrong model of the ids it counts

Rendered string in Help's identifier table, row 1, measured live:

    T- | a work item | 115 | minted by aim task new; the store is the authority

The count is `board.tasks.length` (`HelpPane.vue:29,34-35`). The live payload has
**115** tasks of which **87** are `provenance: "seed only (not yet in the store)"` and
**28** are `store only` — with the same `T-` prefix and disjoint id ranges (seeds
`T-0001..T-0155`, store `T-0156..T-0183`).

Both clauses of the sentence are therefore false for 87 of the 115 ids it counts:
those were not minted by `aim task new`, and the store is not their authority because
the store has no record of them. Help never mentions `provenance`, never gives the two
ranges, and never says a seed cannot be moved, assigned or recorded.

The reader opens Help *because* 115 things look like work, and Help tells him they are
work items minted by `aim task new`. The 87 promises stay invisible as promises, which
is the opposite of Help's job. The concept is already documented in the glossary
(`concept-...`: "a work item that exists in the leader's plan file but has no record in
the store yet") — the identifier row just does not agree with it.

## Acceptance

1. The `T-` row states the split with live counts: how many ids are on the record and
   how many are plan seeds.
2. It carries a sentence to the effect that a plan seed cannot be moved, assigned or
   recorded.
3. It no longer claims every `T-` id came from `aim task new`.
4. Both numbers are derived from `provenance`, so they cannot drift from the payload.

title: Gantt draws 87 plan promises as work and paints 42 of them done
accept: See the card body for the acceptance criteria

body: # Gantt draws 87 promises as work, and paints 42 of them green "done" Measured by a reviewer on `#/gantt` at 1440x1000 and 1024x800, live bundle. Pane header reads: `timeline — 102 of 102 dated item(s), 2026-09-21 → 2026-10-02`. The payload holds 115 tasks: **87 `seed only (not yet in the store)`** and 28 store. Of the 102 that carry dates, **87 are seeds and 15 are on the record**. Bar colour is `color(t.status)` (`GanttPane.vue:72`), so the 44 bars painted `done` are **42 seeds and 2 recorded items**. A seed has **no events**. It has a `start` and a `due` from `plan/plan.json` and nothing else, so those 42 green bars have zero completions behind them. Tooltips do not mention provenance — `rg "provenance|seed" web/src/panes/GanttPane.vue` returns nothing: seed T-0001 Freeze the PM contract… / done · codex · high / 2026-09-21 → 2026-09-21 (3d estimate) / M0 record T-0157 Kanban filters must derive from the URL… / done · claude-session1 · high / 2026-09-22 → 2026-09-22 / M9 The reader sees a 102-row timeline that reads as a record of 102 pieces of work, 85% of which is the plan file restated, with the plan's own status colouring it. That is the T-0180 failure on a surface where it is worse, because a Gantt is the one view whose whole point is that a bar is an interval somebody actually worked. **The fix is already built and used elsewhere.** `isPromise` is exported from `web/src/stores/board.js:62`, `PromiseTag.vue` renders a "planned" chip, and `OverviewPane` uses both — its new promise card already separates the 87 out correctly. `KanbanPane.vue:149` uses a third rendering of the same fact: a raw `plan seed`. `ItemsPane.vue` and `GanttPane.vue` import neither. So there is one predicate and three renderings, and the two panes with none are the two that show the most rows. ## Acceptance 1. On `#/gantt`, exactly the 87 seed bars carry a mark, and their tooltips say the dates are planned rather than recorded. The 15 recorded bars carry no such mark. 2. A promise's bar is not coloured as though the status were an outcome. 3. One component renders this fact on every pane that draws a task — Help, Kanban, Items, Gantt, Plan and Attention agree, and a test asserts the predicate is the same one (`isPromise`), not four copies of `provenance.includes('seed')`.

title: At 1024 the Gantt timeline collapses to 151px and still truncates 88 labels
accept: See the card body for the acceptance criteria

body:
# At 1024px the Gantt's timeline is 151px wide, and 88 of 102 labels are still truncated

Measured by a reviewer on `#/gantt`. Canvas is 722x2272 at 1024x800 and 1138x2272 at
1440x1000.

`yAxis.axisLabel.width` is a hard `470` (`GanttPane.vue:101`), so bars start at canvas
x≈503 at **both** widths:

    1440x1000 : timeline x 503 → 1038 = 535px for 13 day-units ≈ 41px/day
    1024x800  : timeline x 503 →  654 = 151px for 13 day-units ≈ 11.6px/day

A one-day bar is therefore 12–13px long against ~15px of bar thickness — a one-day task
is taller than it is wide. At 1024 the entire 13-day horizon is a 151px strip, so
duration is unreadable, while the label gutter still eats 65% of the chart.

And the gutter does not even buy legible labels: measured with the pane's own font
(`11.5px ui-monospace`), **88 of 102 labels exceed 470px** (median 512px, max 519px)
and are truncated with `…` at both widths. `GanttPane.vue:53` additionally cuts titles
at 62 characters first, so 79 titles were shortened before they ever reached the axis.

Root cause: a fixed pixel gutter (`:101`) and fixed grid margins (`:77`) with only the
height derived from the row count (`:57`). Width is not a function of the container.

This is the second time the leader has called the Gantt unusable, and the previous fix
is documented in the file's own header comment. The remaining defect is geometric, not
stylistic: nothing about the layout responds to the width it is given.

## Acceptance

1. At 1024x800 the timeline is at least 300px wide and the label column is at most 40%
   of the canvas.
2. No label loses more characters at 1024 than at 1440.
3. A test measures both viewports and asserts the timeline fraction, so a fixed pixel
   gutter cannot come back.

title: Plan claims the store wins about 87 disagreements that have no store value
accept: See the card body for the acceptance criteria

body:
# Plan says "the store wins" about 87 disagreements that have no store value at all

`#/plan` renders this, verbatim, measured on the live board:

    plan/*.json is the leader's plan and a seed. The store is the evidence: where the
    two disagree the store wins, and the 87 disagreement(s) are on the attention page.
    13 item(s) have no due date, which in a plan is a sentence without a verb.

All **87** entries in `/api/state.drift` are `{field: "status", store: null}`. Every
one is a seed with **no record at all**, not a disagreement — there is no store value
for the store to win with. So the sentence is false for 100% of the count it states.

And `#/plan` itself renders **0** drift rows. The only evidence is an off-pane link to
`#/attention#drift`, which lands on the 969px card of 20-of-87 rows that this project
has already rejected once (T-0180), and which — separately — does not actually scroll
when clicked (T-0183).

Root cause: `PlanPane.vue:47-54` renders the count and the link but not the rows, fed by
`drift: (s) => s.doc?.drift || []` (`board.js:271`). The payload's `store: null` is
never surfaced as the word "not recorded".

The reader is shown a number presented as conflict-resolution work, which is actually
"87 promises were never recorded".

## Acceptance

1. The wording distinguishes an absent record from a disagreeing value: `store = not
   recorded` for a null store, and the sentence no longer claims the store overrode a
   value that does not exist.
2. The rows are readable where the count is stated — on `#/plan` itself, bounded with a
   stated "M more" if needed — rather than only behind a link.
3. `PromiseTag` marks the seed rows, so the page agrees with the rest of the board.

title: Nothing above a task: no project, no epic, no cycle, and milestones have no pane
accept: The leader chooses (a) a first-class milestone pane plus a cycle object, or (b) a stated decision that this board has no cycle model; whichever is chosen is visible in the payload, the nav and Help

body:
# Nothing on the board sits above a task, so the board is flat by construction

Raised by a reviewer looking at the information architecture. This is the structural
half of the leader's standing complaint — *"就是太混乱了，我打开页面看到一大堆东西，
我不知道看什么。概念太多了"* — and worth deciding before more panes are added.

**Measured.** A recursive scan of `/api/state` finds **no** `project`, `epic`, `cycle`,
`sprint`, `iteration`, `initiative`, `goal` or `objective` key. The only grouping above
a task is `milestone`: 10 objects (`M0`..`M9`, each with `name`/`due`/`accept`) plus a
`milestone` string on each task.

**Milestones have no pane.** They appear as a table inside `Plan & risks`
(`PlanPane.vue:75-93`), as a filter on Work items and Gantt, and as a 4-row card on
Attention. The one object above the task is subordinated to a governance pane that also
holds risks, decisions, non-goals and RACI.

**There is no current cycle.** `reports` is a date-indexed burndown (`series`),
`throughput`, and per-item `cycle_days`/`median_cycle` — measures of how long things
took, not an iteration with a start, an end and a commitment. Nothing on the board
answers "what are we doing this cycle, and what is the goal".

**So three of ten nav items render the same flat list.** Kanban, Gantt and Work items
are three views of one task array. Every mature tool in this space separates at least
two levels above a task — a project or epic, and a timebox — and the reason is not
decoration: without them, "is this project healthy" has no answer, only "how many of
the 115 rows are green".

This is a design question with two defensible answers and I want the leader's call
rather than a guess:

- **(a)** Promote milestones to a first-class pane (one self-registering file in
  `web/src/views/`) and add a cycle object to `plan/plan.json` and `/api/state`.
- **(b)** Declare that this tool has no cycle model on purpose — it is a task board with
  a barrier, not a delivery tracker — and say so in Help, so the flatness is a stated
  design rather than an omission.

(a) is what a PM tool is judged on; (b) is cheaper and honest. Either is better than the
current state, which is flat and says nothing about being flat.

## Acceptance

Once the leader picks: `/api/state` exposes whatever level was chosen with a name and a
time bound; the nav has one item landing on it; the landing route shows it; and Help
explains it in the same words the rest of the board uses.

Second measured symptom of the same root cause, reported by a reviewer on the live
board at 1280x800. This one is about a route change, not a fragment.

    #/items scrolled to the bottom (scrollTop 4787/4787) -> click nav "Help & concepts"
      -> #/help, .aim-main scrollTop 3937/3937  (the BOTTOM of a 4688px page, in the glossary)

    #/help scrolled to the bottom -> click nav "Attention"
      -> #/attention, scrollTop 1435/1435  (the bottom, on the 87-row drift card)

Reproduced twice, same numbers. The scroll container is `.aim-main.aim-main`
(`App.vue:120`), and `main.js:48-58` builds the router with no `scrollBehavior`, so
nothing resets it on navigation.

So the reader clicks "Help" to clear up the wall of numbers and arrives at the bottom of
a 4564px glossary; or clicks "Attention" and lands on the drift wall he was trying to
get away from. That is worth stating in the acceptance for this card: a route change
must leave the destination scrolled to the top, and only a fragment should scroll
further.

title: Audit & barrier: one heading over 5400px, and the leader's only action is 4000px down
accept: The page states its purpose in one sentence, is ordered barrier-first and evidence-second, its leader action is above the fold, sealed claims are collapsed, and empty sections are one line

body:
# Audit & barrier has one heading over 5400px, and its one action is at the very bottom

The leader's words: *"audit and barrier 这个页面我他妈根本没看懂，他妈的乱七八糟的，我
根本不知道你这个页面是干什么的"*. He is right, and the page can be described
precisely. Measured on `http://127.0.0.1:8799/#/barrier` (which auto-selects
`?channel=barrier-v0`), viewer `human`, 1440x1000:

    scroller            951px visible, 5400px of content, 10,235 characters
    headings on the page exactly one: "Audit & barrier"
    tabs                5 channels, active = #barrier-v0 — Synthesising
    selects             15  (three filters — agent / class / phase — repeated per tab)
    buttons             5, every one of them labelled "clear"

Sections inside the active tab, with their positions:

    y=   0  h= 166   el-descriptions      topic, leader, phase, round, participants, counts
    y= 180  h= 287   the chain            every file the record is made of
    y= 481  h=3931   seals                a digest each participant committed to, before reading the peer
    y=4426  h= 497   refusals             0 of 0 record(s) — "No Data", with three filter selects
    y=4937  h= 284   phase history        only the leader moves it

## Why it reads as a mess

1. **One heading over 5400px.** Four cards, no section headings, and no sentence
   anywhere saying what the page is for. The nav calls it "Audit & barrier", which
   names two different jobs, and the page then does a third thing (the chain) and a
   fourth (phase history) without ever saying how they relate.
2. **The largest object is the least actionable.** The seals card is **3931px, 73% of
   the page**, and it lays out both participants' full sealed claims — statement,
   `confidence`, and "would change my mind" — as flat table rows. That is a reading
   task, not a decision, and it is the first thing a reader scrolls into.
3. **The one thing that needs the leader is last.** The phase card is the only place a
   human can act, its own heading says "only the leader moves it", and it sits at
   y=4937 — five screens down, past 4000px of material he cannot act on.
4. **A section that is empty takes 497px.** Refusals shows "0 of 0 record(s)" and
   "No Data", under three filter dropdowns. An empty table with filters is the page
   telling the reader to filter something that does not exist.
5. **It opens on the least relevant channel.** The active tab is `barrier-v0`, the
   first alphabetically — a research channel whose sealed claims are the 3931px. The
   channel the project actually works in (`hello`) is the third tab. Four of the five
   channels are scaffolding (`T-0177`), and nothing on the page says so.
6. **The vocabulary is never introduced.** "the chain", "seals", "refusals", "phase
   history", "concessions", "round", "digest" — nine terms, none defined here. Help
   defines some of them, and there is no link from where they are used to where they
   are explained (`T-0185`).

## What the page is actually for, and the order it should be in

It serves two different readers and does neither first:

- **The barrier** — what phase this channel is in, what that permits right now, and
  the leader's single move. That belongs first, above the fold, with the advance
  control on it.
- **The audit** — the evidence behind the phase: the chain's integrity, the seals, the
  refusals. That belongs second, collapsed by default, entered on request.

`el-collapse` and `el-table`'s expandable rows are already available in the installed
`element-plus@2.14.6` (27,778 stars); the sealed claim text belongs behind a per-claim
expander rather than laid flat.

## Acceptance

1. The page states in one sentence what it is for, and its sections are headed and
   ordered barrier-first, evidence-second.
2. The leader's action for the current channel is reachable without scrolling at
   1440x1000, and the page says which channel it applies to.
3. The sealed claims do not occupy more than one screen in their default state.
4. An empty section renders as one line, not as a table with filters.
5. The page does not open on a channel with no work when a channel with work exists,
   and a scaffolding channel says it is scaffolding.
6. The first occurrence of each of the nine terms links to its Help row.

tasks carry one provenance value each; drift is empty or every entry names the
action that clears it; a test asserts no task is reachable under two provenances.
`imported_from` records where each item came from. Add `--dry-run`.

Seed evidence for the claim: T-0070's title is "Record every work item of this
project as a task in the fabric, not in a chat window" and its provenance is
`seed only (not yet in the store)`.

design/12-architecture-review.md §1.3. The leader's standing complaint is "I see
T-004, and I don't know how to act on it". Today that is literally true.

Measured on the served bundle (assets/index-kt71uWBo.js, viewer human): the
overview promise row for T-0004 reads
  `T-0004 Leader: approve the plan; advance hello past SEALED_DIVERGENT planned decision for you`
its only control is `["open it"]`, and the drawer it opens offers
`["Start doing", "Record this work item"]` — no Approve / Request changes /
Reject, because the item is a seed and is not in the store.
Source: web/src/panes/OverviewPane.vue:233,242,243 and
web/src/components/TaskDecisionDrawer.vue:219,260,273,308.

Acceptance: every Decision and every WorkItem in /api/state carries `actions[]`,
each `{label, argv, why}` with the viewer already substituted and any `--as`
dropped (the rule T-0141 established). A test walks the payload and fails if a
primary control has no argv. A row that says "decision for you" must be
approvable from that row.

Do NOT make this a second write path: actions are argv for the one server-side
runner. Render them as buttons; run them through the same executor.

Leader, this session: "整个 estimation 也不对啊，你们作为 llm，任务不是按天算的，应该是按照小时算的吧。"

He is right, and the current state is worse than a wrong unit — it is an
undeclared unit, rendered three different ways:
  store field: `estimate_pts`            bin/aim:1397 (write), bin/aim:2842 (arg)
  Kanban:      `{{ t.estimate }}d`       web/src/panes/KanbanPane.vue:125
  Gantt:       `(${t.estimate}d estimate)` web/src/panes/GanttPane.vue:84
  Items:       label `est`, no unit      web/src/panes/ItemsPane.vue:79
  plan seeds:  1..5  (33x2, 24x3, 18x1, 6x5, 1x4)

Change: one declared unit, `estimate_hours` (integer). Render `4h` everywhere; a
surface that cannot state the unit renders nothing rather than a bare number.
Gantt bar width derives from hours, not from a `start`..`due` day span. Keep
`start`/`due` at day granularity only for calendar-shaped commitments.

Migration rule, stated once and recorded in the note: `1 pt = 1 h`, applied to
the seeds and existing items by one script, never by hand — a hand-migrated
number is an invented number. Acceptance: no surface renders a unitless
estimate, and the conversion rule is in the record.

title: Insight report: a 10-minute flow chart of opened vs done, in hours
accept: 10-minute buckets over a selectable window show opened and done counts and hours; the longest idle gap is named; an import burst is distinguishable from work; no figure is unitless

body:
Leader, this session: the insight report must show hours, and a 10-minute-bucket
trend of done vs newly opened, so he can judge whether the workflow is saturated.

The data exists — I measured it before filing, from channels/*/tasks.jsonl:
  151 event records, all timestamped: created 63, moved 35, commented 28,
  assigned 15, published 8, retracted 1, dropped 1.
Bucketing `created` and `moved->done` at 10 minutes over the whole record:

  bucket  open  done
   02:10     1     0
   02:40     1     0
   02:50     5     0
   03:00     9     2
   03:20     6     0
   03:30     4     0
   03:40     3     0
   03:50     1     0
   07:10    33     0
  TOTAL     63     2

Two things that chart already tells you, and one that would have told you a lie:

1. The stream is bursty and one-sided: 63 opened, 2 closed, 9 active buckets, and
   a silent gap from 03:50 to 07:10. That gap is the real finding — an idle window
   is invisible today.

   An import is not work, and a chart that cannot tell them apart will report a

   reached `done` through a recorded `moved` event — the rest inherit it from
   plan/plan.json seeds. Until T-0210 lands, this chart reads "the workflow is
   idle" while work is happening. Do not ship the chart without saying which
   authority the `done` series came from.
