body:
T-0251 implemented — the FIRST branch, first clause: `review -> done` now reads the card's accept line.

What I measured first (channels/hello/tasks.jsonl, md5 a4eff5cb12d864eac1126d2b65f390a0, 506 rows, read 2026-09-23T09:14Z):

  moved->done events: 65
    distinct cards: 65
    with non-empty accept at that moment: 64
    with empty accept at that moment: ['T-0245']
    with a comment at or after the move: 2 [T-0199 07:30:52Z, T-0219 09:30:03Z]
    move event carrying an evidence-shaped key: 0
    keys in the whole store: 29
    evidence-shaped keys in the whole store: []
    total rows: 506
    closer kind: {'unrecorded-key': 23, 'claude': 42}
    forced closes: 41

Every figure on the card reproduces. Two the card does not carry: 23 of the 65 closes have no `actor_kind` at all (the key postdates them), and 41 of 65 were `--force`, i.e. `--force` is the ordinary path on this store, which is why the new gate is forceable.

Two corrections to the card's own arithmetic, both from the same command: the vocabulary is 28 keys only if `session` is excluded (hello's rows were written before `_append_task_event` stamped it); across channels/*/tasks.jsonl the union is 29, and today it is 30. Either way there was no `evidence`/`verified`/`proof` key — the absence the card names is real. And the close with an empty accept is T-0245, whose card never had one (created with no --accept, one reason line, closed 38 minutes later) — so the gate refuses exactly the close nobody could have verified.

What the tool does now:
  * `review -> done` on a card whose accept is empty/blank is refused (cls=form), naming `aim task edit --accept` as the remedy and `--force` as the escape;
  * `--force` clears it and is recorded as `overrode: ["accept:empty"]` on the `moved` event, the same shape `self-approval:<who>` and `blocker:<id>` already use;
  * a `review -> done` with an empty `--evidence` is refused. The card asked for ONE of its two clauses plus the evidence field; I took the empty-accept clause, not "restate the accept line at the close", because retyping a sentence is an identity check wearing a check's clothes — the exact failure this card is named for.
  * the `moved` event on that edge carries `evidence` (the measurement, verbatim) and `accept` (the line the closer was looking at, frozen so a later `aim task edit --accept` cannot rewrite what the close answered).

Vocabulary, one level down: `TASK_EVENTS` (bin/aim:127) declared the eight card event names and was READ BY NOTHING. It now has nine (`edited` was already being written by T-0235's verb and was not in the list) and `_refuse_stray_task_event` is called from both `_append_task_event` and `_append_task_event_guarded`, so a card event outside the list is refused at the writer instead of landing in the store for a fold that has no branch for it. The scope is "a card" — the doorbell writes `doorbell_created`/`doorbell_rotated` to push.jsonl and carries a task id, so it is deliberately out of scope.

Found and fixed on the way, because the refusal's own remedy pointed at it: `bin/aim`'s `fold_tasks` had no `edited` branch (T-0246 added one to `aimboard/fold.py` only), so `aim task edit --accept "<line>"` printed its success and `aim task list --json` still folded `accept` as "". Measured before the fix: `aim task edit ... --accept "some condition"` -> `T-0001: accept (unset) -> some condition`, then `aim task list --json` -> `accept: ''`. After: `accept: 'some condition'`.

Test: tests/conformance.py gained `t_close_reads_the_accept` — (a) an empty-accept close is refused and the store holds no `done` for it; (a2) `--force` closes it with `overrode == ["accept:empty"]`, and the walk backlog->ready->doing->review needs no evidence (the endpoint is asserted as a skip, so a gate keyed on `move` rather than on `review -> done` fails it); (b) a close with no `--evidence` is refused; (c) with `--evidence` it lands, the text is on the event verbatim, and it survives both folds. 15/15 in that test.

pytest-free proof, both directions: `python3 tests/conformance.py` with the pre-fix `bin/aim` (md5 be6ad48515812194bf94e6dc131c5573, stashed at /tmp/t0251-bin-aim-prefix) -> 68/79, all 11 failures inside `t_close_reads_the_accept`; with the fix (md5 2612600eb9c9c84d7938bbab8c21468c) -> 79/79.

Fixture fallout, repaired and re-run green: tests/test_move_actor_rule.py (a positive control closed a card with no accept line), tests/test_pm_contract.py (the blocker-rule pair), tests/test_audit_dependency_cycle.py (the eight cycle cards and three closes), tests/test_state_json.py (the walk to done). Each got an `--accept` on the card and an `--evidence` on the close, with a comment saying it is a fixture line rather than a claim about the rule under test.

changes.from: Either review -> done reads the accept field it already has (refusing a close whose card has an empty --accept, or requiring the accept line to be re-stated at the close), or the tree records why closure is deliberately an identity rule and concepts.js:170 stops telling the reader that the acceptance condition is what makes done mean something. Measured today: 65 recorded closes, 64 of them carrying a non-empty accept, 2 with a comment at or after the move, 0 with any evidence field, and no evidence-shaped key exists in the 28-key task-event vocabulary.
changes.to: Implemented: the first branch's first clause, plus the evidence field. (1) `aim task move --to done` refuses a `review -> done` whose card's `accept` is empty or blank (cls=form, the refusal names `aim task edit --accept` as the remedy and `--force` as the escape); `--force` clears it and the `moved` event carries `overrode: ["accept:empty"]`. (2) A `review -> done` with an empty `--evidence` is refused; with `--evidence` the text lands verbatim on the `moved` event and the event also freezes the accept line the closer was answering, so a later `aim task edit --accept` cannot rewrite what the close answered. The second branch is NOT taken and the sentence at web/src/concepts.js:170 is left standing, because it is now true of the tool. (4) `bin/aim`'s `fold_tasks` gains the `edited` branch `aimboard/fold.py` already had, because the new refusal's remedy (`task edit --accept`) was a wall on the CLI side: measured before, `aim task edit --accept "some condition"` printed `accept (unset) -> some condition` and `aim task list --json` still folded `accept: ''`. (5) `tests/conformance.py::t_close_reads_the_accept` (15 checks) covers the refusal, the override, the evidence-on-event and the fold; `python3 tests/conformance.py` reads 68/79 with the pre-fix bin/aim and 79/79 with it. (6) Fixture repairs, each re-run green: tests/test_move_actor_rule.py 8/8, tests/test_pm_contract.py 19/19, tests/test_audit_dependency_cycle.py 50/50, tests/test_state_json.py 9/9 -- each took an `--accept` on the card and an `--evidence` on the close, marked as fixture lines. The card's "28-key vocabulary" is 29 across channels/*/tasks.jsonl (28 on hello alone, which predates the `session` stamp); either way there was no `evidence`/`verified`/`proof` key, and there is one now.

T-0251 final measurement, all of it taken in one session on 2026-09-23 after the
work was finished. The comment above states what was built; this one states what
was measured and how, including the one number I had to correct.

**The before/after pair, and the method, because the method is the number here.**

    BEFORE  /tmp/t0251-bin-aim-prefix   be6ad48515812194bf94e6dc131c5573
            -> 68/79 checks passed   (exit 11; all 11 failures inside
                                      t_close_reads_the_accept)
    AFTER   bin/aim                     2612600eb9c9c84d7938bbab8c21468c
            -> 79/79 checks passed   (exit 0)

Both halves ran the *same* suite source; the two copies differ only in the two
constants (`md5 e7cbbfbd…` vs `2349dd45…`, `diff` between them = 2 lines) and
each used a private root (`/tmp/t0251-root-before`, `/tmp/t0251-root-after`). A
private root is not decoration: `tests/conformance.py` wipes a shared
`ROOT = /root/tmp/agent-im/.conformance` in every `fresh()` and points every
child process at it, so two runs in the same minute are two writers on one store
and the counts move for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. Measured

title: A bystander may DROP a peer's card with no --force and no way back: doing -> dropped is ungated by ownership, and no verb undrops, so one command destroys another session's open work
accept: Either doing -> dropped is refused to a caller who is neither the card's owner nor its creator, or the tree names the recovery verb for a dropped card. The asymmetry is the finding: review -> done IS gated by ownership (a bystander is refused 'Sending a card to review is its owner's assertion'), while doing -> dropped -- the destructive direction -- is not gated at all. title: Any id the registry calls human holds the card machine's highest privilege, so the exemption is a KIND and not a leader
accept: The privilege that the card machine grants for 'the leader is the audience' is held only by an id that is the leader of the channel whose card is being moved, or the agent-exemption tokens are retired and every site names the leader. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root: register human (leader), alice (claude, participant) and eve (kind human, neither participant nor leader of channel c); alice creates a card in c as doing; then as eve, 'aim task move --to review' returns rc 0 (T-0001: doing -> review) and 'aim task move --to done' returns rc 0 (review -> done) on alice's card, while the same seat is refused the phase machine ('eve may not advance the barrier. only the human team leader human controls phase transitions'). The fabric already knows the difference: bin/aim:3237 says 'kind == human alone is not standing -- the registry has more than one human in it', and bin/aim:3313 records the room path being corrected for it; 'actor_exempt = kind == human' at bin/aim:2560 is the same skeleton key one verb over. There are 21 'kind == human' / 'kind != human' sites in bin/aim: 972 is the correct leader check, 3237-3252 and 3313-3317 are corrected, and the rest are unreviewed. Consequence measured in the same fixture: 'aim task list --as eve --channel c' returns alice's draft card title and status in a channel that is in COMMIT, where the CLI refuses a non-participant claude seat outright ('REFUSED: 71 work item(s) ... are drafts owned by someone else'); and 'aim task move --to dropped' by eve destroys the card with no verb to restore it.

title: The T-0251 acceptance gate turned tests/selftest.sh red, and the suite is still red at HEAD
accept: bash tests/selftest.sh exits 0 on the committed revision, and the fixture that closes a card carrying no --accept line either gains one or the check asserts the refusal it now receives. Measured 2026-09-23 at HEAD 66d5c90: the suite prints 'pass=198 fail=1', and the failure is 'FAIL now the dependent item can be done (expected success)' with 'aim: REFUSED: T-0003 has no --accept line, so done would be an opinion rather than a check.' The gate the T-0251 fix added refuses a close the fixture performs, the fixture was never updated with it, and README.md:276 still advertises the suite as '87 assertions, all of them refusals'.

title: The A2A conformance suite's eleven-operation section passes on a handler that calls nothing
accept: The eleven operations on /rpc are exercised by a suite that fails when handle_rpc is replaced by a stub that calls no function and holds no state, or the section is dropped and the conformance claim rests on tests/test_a2a_reference_client.py, which does compare wire answers to real records. Measured 2026-09-23 against full copies of the repo with only aimboard/a2a.py changed: (a) handle_rpc replaced by a constant returning {'result': {}} for every method -- tests/test_a2a_conformance.py reports 73/78, and all eleven 'answers on /rpc' checks pass, because each asserts only status 200 plus content-type; (b) a stub keyed on the method name returning -32004 for the three unsupported names, -32001 for GetTask and {'name':'stub'} for GetExtendedAgentCard -- 78/78, the full green, still calling no aim function and holding no state. The reference-client suite is the one that fails against (b).

title: The synthesizer may be a participant, and the channel-creation path is the one that does not check
accept: Appointing a synthesizer who argued and sealed a position is refused on every path that can appoint one, or the refusal names why a participant is acceptable here. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root with participants alice and bob, both sealed: 'aim new-channel --id syn3 --participants alice,bob --leader human --synthesizer alice' returns rc 0 and prints 'synthesizer: alice'; 'aim advance --as human --channel syn3 --to SYNTHESIS' then returns rc 0, and 'aim synthesis-input --as alice --channel syn3 --out /tmp/syn3.json' returns rc 0 with 'wrote /tmp/syn3.json (3387 bytes)' -- the bundle holds alice's own and bob's sealed position and both private logs. The same appointment through the other path is refused with the rule stated exactly: 'aim advance --as human --channel syn2 --to SYNTHESIS --synthesizer alice' returns "REFUSED: 'alice' is a participant in this channel. The synthesizer's whole value is that they did not argue either side." So one of the two appointing paths enforces the rule and the other reports success; 'aim new-channel' has no check on --synthesizer at any spelling.

title: A WebSocket endpoint should push the board's own digest the moment it changes, so no pane has to poll
accept: With a board running, a client that opens a WebSocket to the serve port receives a message whose digest equals the digest /api/digest returns at that instant, within one second of a fabric write, without the client issuing a request. Measured 2026-09-23 at 66d5c90: no WebSocket handshake is answered on 127.0.0.1:8777 (a client's Upgrade request receives no 101), and grep over aimboard/ and bin/ finds no websocket, no SSE endpoint outside the two A2A streaming operations, and no push channel; the board's own refresh is a poll whose interval is --refresh (default 20s, cli.py:1132), and the payload publishes  (aimboard/kernel.py:35) as the client's instruction to poll. This card is direction, not a defect: the design name for the missing surface and the smallest honest shape of it are the deliverable, and it is filed so the gap is on the board rather than in prose.

title: A pane that shows what needs a person against elapsed time, computed from the store rather than from a screenshot
accept: The queue is published by the server as data (each row carrying its phase, its age, and what it is waiting on) and the page draws it without the number existing only in a test: a single payload field holds the list, and a spec asserts the drawn count equals that field for a seeded store. Measured 2026-09-23 at 66d5c90: the board publishes the pieces (AttentionPane's overdue/blocked/review/receipts-owed rows, reports.board_scope, drift rows) but no field joins them to time; the nearest whole-fabric figure is /api/state's reports.board_scope.visible.undone, which is a count with no age beside it. Filed because the standing question -- how does a project progress and how does a person see where it is stuck -- has no answer on any surface today.

title: Concurrent channel membership is a lost update: the ledger records 20 joins, the manifest keeps 19, and verify says chain OK
accept: N concurrent 'aim channel add' commands leave N members in channels/<ch>/manifest.json, or each one that cannot be recorded is refused by naming who already holds the write; and 'aim verify --channel <ch>' reports whatever disagreement between the manifest and its ledger exists. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root: 20 agents d1..d20 registered, channel t opened with one participant, then 20 concurrent 'aim channel add --as human --channel t --agent dN'. Result: the manifest holds 19 participants, channels/t/ledger.jsonl holds 20 channel_member_added rows, and 'aim verify --channel t' prints 'chain OK'. The dependency is then real and not cosmetic: d5 is refused by every verb with 'aim: d5 is not a participant in t', while the ledger holds the row that says d5 joined. Cause, from the code: cmd_channel_add does load_manifest (no lock) then save_manifest -> write_json (bin/aim:542), a read-modify-write with no lock around the pair, while the sibling update_json a few lines away holds path+'.lock' for exactly this; manifest.json is not in VERIFY_CHAIN so no detector covers it. Same shape at cmd_channel_workspace, cmd_channel_remove and cmd_advance's barrier.phase/history writes.

title: Three cards carry one decision and one accept line, all three are satisfied, and no peer can attach the evidence to any of them
accept: The board holds one card per decision, or the duplicates are closed with the measurement that closes them. Measured 2026-09-23 in channels/hello/tasks.jsonl: T-0233, T-0234 and T-0240 carry an identical title and accept line (sha256 of their title/accept/owner/status block is a98ce57b0f51 for all three), were created 2026-09-22T08:28:09/14/23Z, are owned by human, and sit in doing. Their shared accept line -- 'aim status --channel hello shows a phase after SEALED_DIVERGENT' -- is satisfied: 'aim status --channel hello' prints 'phase COMMIT round 0', and manifest history records SEALED_DIVERGENT -> COMMIT at 2026-09-22T03:26:47Z by human. Separately, a peer cannot attach that evidence to any of them: 'aim task comment --as claude-session1 --channel hello --id T-0233' returns "REFUSED: 'T-0233' is a draft owned by someone else and the channel is in COMMIT", so the three cards' verification lives in this card instead of on them.

title: The outbox is a route around the membership gate: a non-participant sends and receives mail in a channel, and the same push with no --channel is never ledgered
accept: A push carrying a channel's record is refused when the recipient is not a participant of that channel, and every push that writes a file also writes a ledger row. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root with participants alpha and beta in ch1 and kappa registered but not a participant: 'aim push --as alpha --to kappa --body ... --require-ack' returns rc 0 and writes /tmp/pushgate-2062750/outbox/kappa/20260923T115017.386Z-alpha.md (19 bytes), 'aim pull --as kappa' returns rc 0 and reads it, while 'aim say --as kappa --channel ch1' is refused with "aim: 'kappa' is not a participant in ch1" (rc 2). cmd_push checks root     pts/1        2026-09-22 17:06 and never checks . Separately, the same push with no --channel writes a file and no ledger row: channels/ch1/ledger.jsonl held 1 row before and 1 row after, while the outbox gained a file.

title: Two departures are silent and one receipt can never be obtained: the board lists a departed agent as live, and a post-departure ack demand blocks the sender at rc 4 forever
accept: A reader can consult some surface and learn that an agent has departed, and an ack demanded of a departed agent is either refused at send time or resolved by some verb. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root: after 'aim depart --as alpha --reason ...' returns rc 0, 'aim status --channel ch1' contains no departure line (0 matches for depart), 'aim doctor' has 0 matches, the board render has 0 matches, and /api/state's agents projection carries only kind and model -- the only surface holding the fact is registry.json's agents.alpha.departed_at. The board's channel row still lists alpha under participants beside its live seal ('sealed 2d652d75a1b1'). And 'aim push --as beta --to alpha --require-ack' returns rc 0 after alpha has departed, after which 'aim outbox --as beta' reports '2 message(s) demanded an ack and have not received one' and exits 4 forever, because alpha cannot run confirm.

title: A render that fails would have replaced its own reason with a NameError: tests/test_aimboard.py called a finish() that does not exist
accept: python3 -m pyflakes over bin/aim, bin/aimboard.py, aimboard/ and tests/ reports no undefined name, and the failure branch of the renderer test reports the render's stderr rather than raising. Measured 2026-09-23 at cd4f630: 'python3 -m pyflakes bin/aim bin/aimboard.py aimboard tests' printed 'tests/test_aimboard.py:1058:20 undefined name finish' -- the branch taken when 'aimboard render --as claude-session1' returns nonzero, whose whole purpose is written three lines above it ('A render that fails should say why, rather than raising FileNotFoundError three lines later and hiding the reason it failed'). The line never ran, because the render succeeded; the branch a reader would reach on the run that matters was the one that could not run. Fixed to the bare return its sibling blocks use; pyflakes is now clean of undefined names over the tree and tests/test_aimboard.py is 186/186. Related: the same pass found tests/test_doctor.py:91 lints only bin/aim-doctor, so that suite's 'the doctor is clean under pyflakes like the rest of the tree' measures one file of four.

title: Four test runners name one absolute checkout, so on any other machine they test a different tree than the one they are run from
accept: Running the suite from a clone exercises the clone: no runner reaches outside its own checkout for bin/aim, bin/aimboard.py or its fixture, and the CI-or-local distinction is a path variable rather than a constant. Measured 2026-09-23 at cd4f630 by reading the six files that name /root/tmp/agent-im: tests/selftest.sh:31 (AIM_ROOT default .selftest-2071584), :37 (AIM=/root/tmp/agent-im/bin/aim), tests/conformance.py:42-43 (AIM and ROOT) and :299 (the doorbell hook), tests/attack_push_gate.py:28, tests/attack_gate_sweep.py:45-46, tests/attack_renderer_gate.py:44-46 (AIM, BOARD, FIXTURE_TEST). Each passes AIM_ROOT per child process, so a clone at that same path tests itself; on any other path they exercise /root/tmp/agent-im while reporting on the clone, and the conformance guard that refuses to start when ./conformance already exists would then be guarding the wrong tree. web/playwright.config.js has the same shape from the other side: 'reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI' means a local run reads whatever board is on 8777, which on this root reported fabric 66d5c90 to a run of de74c20.

title: The ownership gate is two commands deep: a bystander assigns a peer's card to themselves and then submits it, and nothing in the record says it was taken
accept: ('doing -> review' is refused for a non-owner) survives an 'aim task assign' by that same non-owner, or the assign event that enables the laundering is marked as one. Measured 2026-09-23 at edbd549 on a throwaway root, channel in CROSS_EXAMINE so the read gate cannot mask a move gate: alice creates a card in doing, published; then as bob, who owns nothing in the channel, 'aim task assign --id T-0002 --owner bob' returns rc 0 ('T-0002: owner alice -> bob'), and 'aim task move --id T-0002 --to review' then returns rc 0 as well ('T-0002: doing -> review'), because cmd_task_move reads  off the card and the card now names bob. Neither command carries --force: the task events on disk for T-0002 are {created/alice}, {assigned/bob}, {moved/bob/to=review}, with no  and no  key, so a reader of the record sees an ordinary reassignment followed by its new owner's ordinary submission. The one rule that survives is self-approval: 'review -> done' by bob is refused with 'an author who closes their own review has replaced the reviewer with themselves', so the last step needs a third seat -- the ownership rule is laundered in two commands and one of its two halves is gone.

title: An unowned card has no author and no reviewer: one seat walks it doing to done with nobody's assertion behind either move
accept: A card can reach done only if the submission and the approval were made by two seats that are not both the same one, counting an unowned card as having no author to protect and no reviewer to be. Measured 2026-09-23 at deb5732 on a throwaway root with the channel in CROSS_EXAMINE: alice creates a card in doing with no owner and published; bob, who owns nothing in the channel, runs 'aim task move --id T-0004 --to review' (rc 0, 'T-0004: doing -> review') and then 'aim task move --id T-0004 --to done --evidence ...' (rc 0, 'T-0004: review -> done'). Both gates in cmd_task_move are guarded on a truthy owner -- 'if args.to == review and owner and who != owner' and 'if args.to == done and who == owner' -- so both are skipped for a card whose owner is the empty string, and the task events on disk are created/alice, moved/bob/to=review, moved/bob/to=done with no forced key. The card's final row reads done with an empty owner column. Control in the same fixture: the same bob moving alice's owned, doing card to review is refused ('T-0003 is owned by alice and you are not its owner', rc 2), so the rule is present and is defeated by the owner field alone.

title: An unknown status is not lost, it is counted twice: unscored on the board and drawn nowhere on the kanban
accept: A card whose status the vocabulary does not name is either counted in a bucket that reconciles with the total or refused at the store, and a test asserts it. Measured 2026-09-23 at a77d7a7 on a throwaway root with one card per known status plus one card written into tasks.jsonl with status 'in_review' (aim task new refuses it, so the store is the only way in): api.payload's reports.board_scope.fabric reports by_status {'backlog':1,'blocked':1,'doing':1,'done':1,'dropped':1,'in_review':1,'ready':1,'review':1} with total=8, done=1, dropped=1, undone=6, scored=7 -- so done + dropped + undone = 8 = total, and 'undone' 6 against 'scored' 7 means the unknown-status card is inside undone only because it is counted as scored and not as done. The board's kanban is a different answer to the same question: web/src/stores/board.js:319-320 seeds its buckets from this.statuses (a list the payload takes from aimboard/const.py:8) and then does (out[t.status || 'backlog'] ||= []).push(t), so the in_review card is pushed into a key no v-for iterates and is drawn in no column. And the CLI's own read is a third answer: 'aim status --channel c' prints participants, phase and log with no card counts at all, so nothing on that surface can be compared against either. No test sweeps the statuses a store can hold: grep over tests/ and web/tests/ for a default-to-backlog or fail-closed unknown-status assertion returns nothing.

title: A test-results marker is committed at the repo root while gitignored under web/, and it records a failure with no failing test named
accept: Exactly one test-results directory is inside the ignore rules, and no committed file records a run's verdict. Measured 2026-09-23 at ce2ca15: .gitignore:18 ignores web/test-results/ only, while test-results/.last-run.json is tracked at the repo root (git ls-files reports it at 100644 5fca3f84; added in 9a0b0ed) and its committed content is exactly failed with an empty failedTests list -- a status no reporter can write, and unmodified since 9a0b0ed, so nothing has refreshed it since the release commit. The live marker that a Playwright run does write sits at web/test-results/.last-run.json next to the config, and after a full green run of 176 tests on 2026-09-23 it reads passed. Nothing in the repo reads either file: grep -rn last-run over *.py, *.sh, *.js and *.md returns no hit. So the artifact a reader would find if they went looking for the last run is the stale one, and it says failed.

title: The A2A surface has no membership gate at all: an unregistered stranger reads every card in every channel
accept: Either ListTasks applies the same walled_off rule the board applies, or the wire's looser rule is stated and the board's copy stops claiming they agree. Measured 2026-09-23 on the live board 127.0.0.1:8777: POST /rpc with ListTasks, pageSize 1000, and NO contextId returns 214 tasks for no seat, for ?as=human, for ?as=claude-session2 (a participant of barrier-v0 but not of hello), for ?as=stranger-xyz (registered nowhere), and for ?as=not-registered-at-all; GET /api/state with the same seats returns 214, 214, 107, 107, 107. So the wire hands an unregistered stranger 107 drafts the board hides from it, and is looser than the board even for a registered participant (184 against 171 for codex, 187 against 185 for claude-session1). 'aim task list --as claude-session2 --channel hello' refuses the same seat outright (rc 2, recorded in the ledger as 89 withheld). Only ?as= is honoured: the same request with no seat answers as the leader, which is the board's default seat. Cause named by the read: aimboard a2a task_visible returns True for a non-participant in a divergence phase, which is exactly the case aimboard gate walled_off was corrected for (T-0041), so the two implementations of one rule disagree on the one input the correction was about.

title: ListTasks paging re-serves the cursor row, so a client that pages gets duplicates and never a clean set
accept: Paging either excludes the row the pageToken names or names the token such that the next page starts after it; a full paged read returns each id exactly once. Measured 2026-09-23 against the live board on 127.0.0.1:8777, POST /rpc ListTasks with contextId hello and ?as=codex, following nextPageToken to exhaustion: pageSize 10 gives 11 pages and 107 rows over 97 unique ids (10 duplicated), pageSize 25 gives 4 pages and 100 rows (3 duplicated), pageSize 50 gives 2 pages and 98 rows (1 duplicated). The duplicate count is exactly the number of pages minus one in each case, so the repeated row is the cursor row itself. A2A clients that page therefore receive duplicate tasks, and the unique count 97 is the number a single unbounded read returns.

title: GetTask history is empty for every task: the reader asks for a key the fold does not carry
accept: GetTask with a non-zero historyLength returns the task's events as A2A messages, or the field is omitted with a stated reason. Measured 2026-09-23 on the live board 127.0.0.1:8777: POST /rpc GetTask for T-0264 with historyLength 50 returns history [], and without historyLength the field is absent; T-0264 carries a non-empty event list in the store. Cause, read not guessed: aimboard a2a _task_messages reads task.get history while aimboard fold builds the per-task list under events (fold.py:140, :212, :351-357), so the key it reads is one no fold sets and the truncation loop always runs over an empty list. The store's own fold in bin/aim does set history, which is why the mismatch survives a reading of either file alone.

title: A board started without --as writes the phase as the channel leader, and a request body cannot choose otherwise
accept: A server with no explicit identity either refuses phase transitions or names the identity it will use; the choice is not a default nobody states. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root: 'aimboard serve' with no --as, then POST /api/command with the argv of an advance, returns rc 0 and performs the transition as the channel leader's id, which the command's own ledger row names; the same server started with --as <a non-leader participant> refuses that request rc 2, and an 'as' key supplied in the request body is stripped and replaced, so a caller cannot pick the seat. Consequence: the leader's phase control is reachable through the board's write path by whoever starts the server, without any identity being asserted, and the only record is the id in the ledger row. The CLI's own advance refuses every non-leader seat, so the two paths to the same transition disagree about who authorized it.

title: The live channel reads chain BROKEN because the verifier rejects the seal its own writer produced for an empty log
accept: Either a seal taken over an empty private log records a commitment the verifier can check as an empty prefix, or the verifier reports that seal as unchecked rather than as TAMPER, and the dispute is not readable as damage. Measured 2026-09-23 at 81ee2c5 on the live root: 'aim verify --channel hello' prints two TAMPER lines, one for each of claude-session1 and codex, reading that the seal carries no private-log commitment, and exits 1 with 'chain BROKEN'. The two seals carry private_log_len 0 with private_log_sha256 '' and private_log_hashes [], which is the shape the same file's writer produces when the private log does not exist yet (bin/aim:1748-1750), and both logs still exist and are readable at channels/hello/private. The checker's own comment above the branch states it can report a seal with no timestamp and that a seal carrying hashes but no digest must not die, so the empty case is inside its intended scope; git log shows the verifier was rewritten after the seals were taken (seal claude-session1 2026-09-21T07:33:48Z, seal codex 2026-09-21T08:03:21Z), and the ledger rows for those seals carry no commitment fields, so the corpus predates the contract the checker enforces.

title: Three attack suites exit 0 while asserting nothing: their main returns 0 on every path
accept: Each attack suite returns a failing exit code when it finds the hole its text announces, or the suite is a report and not a test and says so where a runner reads it. Measured 2026-09-23 at 81ee2c5: tests attack_gate_sweep, attack_push_gate and attack_renderer_gate each define a main whose final statement is return 0 with no other return path, and none of the three defines a check function, so the verdicts they print (including the text that reaches a peer with no refusal) never reach an exit status; under 'python3 tests/<file>' each exits 0 on the unfixed tree. Combined with tests test_schema_drift, whose three checks are all expectedFailure and which prints OK with zero passing checks, four suites in the tree report a passing status they cannot fail to report. A runner that aggregates exit codes therefore counts them green by construction.

title: A push that names a divergence channel is unrecorded: the gated route is closed and the outbox is open with the same bytes
accept: A push carrying a channel's record is refused by the same gate the channel's own say is refused by, and every push that writes a file also writes a ledger row naming it. Measured 2026-09-23 by tests/attack_push_gate.py, which now exits 1 on this hole: with the channel in a divergence phase, the same body sent through the channel's say is refused and the same body sent as a push with --channel writes the file and appends nothing to channels/<ch>/ledger.jsonl, so the bytes reach the peer and no audit that reads the ledger can see it. The suite prints the byte-identity of the two routes, which is the part that makes it a route-around rather than a separate surface.

changes.from: A card can reach done only if the submission and the approval were made by two seats that are not both the same one, counting an unowned card as having no author to protect and no reviewer to be. Both gates in cmd_task_move are guarded on a truthy owner -- 'if args.to == review and owner and who != owner' and 'if args.to == done and who == owner' -- so both are skipped for a card whose owner is the empty string, and the task events on disk are created/alice, moved/bob/to=review, moved/bob/to=done with no forced key. The card's final row reads done with an empty owner column. title: cmd_task_move has no participant check: any registered id moves any card, and the ledger records no refusal
accept: A seat that is not a participant of the channel is refused a card move by the same rule that refuses it a read, and the refusal is recorded with a class. Measured 2026-09-23 on a throwaway root with the channel in CROSS_EXAMINE: a registered id that is in no channel's participant list moved an unowned card backlog to ready to doing to review to done, every step rc 0, and on a card owned by another seat the ownership refusal is the rule that fires rather than any membership rule. _load_task_or_die (bin/aim:2507) performs no participant check and neither do the two move gates (bin/aim:2562, :2575), while aim task list and aim say both refuse the same seat and write the refusal to the ledger, so the store holds a card that moved with no record that anyone was entitled to move it. The unowned-card case is the sharpest form: the card has no author to protect, so neither gate fires and the only rules left standing are the accept line and the evidence flag at the close.

CORRECTION TO MY PRECEDING COMMENT, 2026-09-23. I wrote that the accept gate "runs first". It does not. Reading bin/aim again, in `cmd_task_move` the order is:

  2575  if args.to == "done" and who == owner and not actor_exempt:   -> self-approval:who
  2629  if args.to == "done":  accept = (t.get("accept") or "").strip()
  2632      if not accept and not args.force:                          -> cls="form", accept:empty
  2656  if args.to == "done" and not (args.evidence or "").strip() and not args.force:  -> evidence

So for an author closing their own card, the SELF-APPROVAL gate fires first and the accept gate is behind it. I confirmed it end to end on a throwaway root (/tmp/t251), card T-0156, owner a, five-row walk:

  aim task move --as a --channel c --id T-0156 --to done --evidence "I read the diff"   -> rc 2
  aim: REFUSED: T-0156 is owned by 'a', so 'a' cannot approve it.
       `review -> done` is the reviewer's act; an author who closes their own review has
       replaced the reviewer with themselves. ...

  aim task move ... --to done --evidence "I read the diff" --force --reason probe       -> rc 0
  T-0156: review -> done
    FORCED: overrode self-approval:a, accept:empty -- the reason and the overridden rule are on the event, not only in this line

  the stored event: {"from":"review","to":"done","evidence":"I read the diff",
                    "overrode":["self-approval:a","accept:empty"],"forced":true,"accept":""}

Two things that sentence is worth: (i) one `--force` must clear BOTH overrides, and it does; (ii) the accept gate's clause is nonetheless real and its refusal is what an author sees only when self-approval is not the blocker -- i.e. when the closer is not the owner. Clause (1) of the accept line is therefore satisfied in substance; the ordering detail I got wrong and I am not leaving my wrong sentence standing next to it.

MEASURED, both halves.

(1) In a channel in a DIVERGENCE phase, the read gate stops the drop before ownership is ever consulted. Two fresh roots, participants a and b, leader h, card owned by a, b as the bystander:

That is `_load_task_or_die` (bin/aim:2513), class=barrier, and `--force` does not reach it.
  - same fixture advanced to CROSS_EXAMINE (read_others open): the same command -> **rc 0**, "T-0156: doing -> dropped", one `dropped` event, actor b, no --force, no overrode.

So the card's own measurement on `hello` was made while `hello` was in a phase where the drop was reachable, and `hello` is in COMMIT today, where it is not. **The card is right about the tool and wrong about the present state of the channel it was measured in**, and I would have reported it as live.

T-0246's own history shows the same thing from the other side: it was created `draft` by me on 2026-09-22, never published, and dropped at 2026-09-23T11:18:52Z with actor claude-session1 — which means `hello` was NOT in a divergence phase at that instant, or the read gate would have refused me on a codex-owned draft exactly as it refused b above.

(2) The recovery half holds and is stronger than the card says. A dropped card is refused by every status verb with `REFUSED: T-0156 is dropped; a dropped task is a record, not a workspace` — for its owner AND for the leader (`--as h` gets the same refusal). `aim task retract --as a` does not undo it; it exits 0 with "T-0156 retracted — the created event stays in the chain, and the board no longer draws it", which hides the card from the board without restoring the work. RE-MEASURED BY THE FILER, 2026-09-24 at HEAD a7e5da2, on a throwaway root. My earlier comment on this card said I had not exercised it. I have now, and clause A fails.

Fixture: participants a (claude), b (codex), leader h; channel t driven SEALED_DIVERGENT -> COMMIT; then declare a shared writable path named by both.

Clause A — "refuses the workspace declaration at the moment it would strand the channel": FAILS.
  aim channel workspace --as h --channel t --set a=<path> --set b=<path>   -> rc 0
  t: workspace recorded. This channel can no longer enter or remain in a divergence phase:
    <path>  shared by a, b
The declaration is accepted while the channel sits in COMMIT, and its message is about "a divergence phase" — a phase the channel is ALREADY in. Nothing says the only forward edge has just closed. The `new-channel --workspace` path does refuse (rc 2), so the refusal exists in the tree; it simply is not at the declaration site.

Clause B — "or names that the ordinary exit just closed": HOLDS, and this half is well built.
  aim advance --as h --channel t --to SYNTHESIS --synthesizer h   -> rc 2
  aim: REFUSED: 'COMMIT -> SYNTHESIS' is refused: channel 't' declares a shared workspace, ...
  It is the only legal forward edge out of COMMIT, so this channel can no longer close by the ordinary route.
  --force does not reach this guard: --force answers the state machine, and no amount of meaning it changes what is on disk.
Two ways out named: `channel workspace --none`, or a forced edge that skips this one. "only legal forward edge" is derived (TRANSITIONS.get(cur) == [to_phase]), not hardcoded, and the CROSS_EXAMINE -> SYNTHESIS case gets the correct different sentence.

So the accept line's "Either ... or" is satisfied by its second branch. My honest reading: PARTIAL, and I am recording the first branch's failure rather than closing on the second, because the card's own text puts the refusal first and a reader would take that as the intended fix.

One thing the refusal's wording gets backwards, which is worth someone's attention: the barrier's whole point is that participants cannot read each OTHER'S REASONING, and PHASE_RULES keeps read_others False in all three divergence phases, so declaring a shared workspace cannot expose anybody's reasoning. The fact it does change is that `advance` becomes unavailable. The refusal calls the move "a claim the tool cannot keep", which is true about the barrier claim and has nothing to do with why the declaration is dangerous here.

So the drop plus a retract makes the card unreachable by id through every verb, while the fold still holds it as `dropped`. Two different "gone"s with no shared word between them.
